signals.topic: Prompt caching writes unseen cache entries past explicit breakpoint, causing 1.25x billing for tokens never read
signals.summary: When using explicit cache_control breakpoint on system block only, warm API calls write additional cache entries past the breakpoint on the user content block. These writes are billed at 1.25x cache-write rate but are never read back on subsequent calls, since the trailing content varies per request. This directly causes monetary loss for users on explicit caching mode.
signals.review_reason: Clear billing impact: users are directly charged 1.25x cache-write rate for tokens that are confirmed never read back, as demonstrated in the issue's own reproduction script. This is not a rare edge case — it occurs on every warm call when using explicit cache_control with only a system-block breakpoint. The user provided concrete token counts (cache_creation=1416 on every warm call) demonstrating systematic overbilling. Count=1 but P0 warranted due to direct financial harm on every matching API call.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Server writes additional cache entries past explicit `cache_control` breakpoint, billing 1.25x for tokens that are never read
source_issues.evidence: Warm calls write ~1416 extra tokens to cache billed at 1.25x but never read back. Confirmed reproducible on SDK 0.102.0 and 0.79.0. Reproduces against direct API (not SDK issue). Users are charged for cache writes that produce no cache reads.

signals.topic: Managed Agents subagent vault_ids not inherited — MCP OAuth calls fail in multi-agent patterns
signals.summary: When a coordinator agent dispatches a subagent via agent_toolset_20260401, vault credentials configured at sessions.create are not forwarded to the subagent's execution context. Any MCP tool call in the subagent requiring OAuth credentials (e.g. Dynamics 365, Microsoft Graph MCP server) fails silently or with auth error. There is no mechanism to pass vault_ids through agent_toolset, making vault-backed MCP tools unusable in any coordinator/subagent split.
signals.review_reason: Blocks the primary use case of agent_toolset_20260401 when combined with vault-backed MCP tools — a documented and recommended secure pattern. Multi-agent pipelines that need to call external APIs from subagents are effectively blocked. No workaround within the managed-agents paradigm; only a complex manual multi-session workaround that loses the unified event stream.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents: vault_ids not inherited by subagents dispatched via agent_toolset — MCP OAuth calls fail
source_issues.evidence: Verified: sessions.create has vault_ids param, agents.create/update have none, agent_toolset_20260401 tool schema has no vault_ids parameter. Subagent MCP calls fail with auth errors while coordinator's own MCP calls succeed with the same vault credential. Workaround of manual multi-session orchestration defeats agent_toolset purpose.

signals.topic: Tool runner infinite loop when appending messages inside loop using official advanced usage pattern
signals.summary: Calling runner.append_messages() inside the tool runner loop sets _messages_modified=True, which causes __run__ to skip auto-append of assistant message + tool result. The next iteration sends a request with no tool result in history, so Claude sees the original question unanswered and makes the same tool call again, causing an infinite loop. The bug is in the official Advanced Usage documentation example.
aliases: advanced usage docs infinite loop bug
signals.review_reason: SDK workflow failure: the official 'Advanced usage' documentation example causes an infinite loop. Users following the documented pattern will have their applications hang indefinitely. The root cause is well-identified in the issue (line 281 of _beta_runner.py skipping auto-append when _messages_modified=True). Confirmed to be a documentation inconsistency — the correct pattern (appending both message and tool_response) is shown in the 'Modifying tool results' example on the same page.

source_issues.title: [Bug] append_messages() inside tool runner loop causes infinite loop (advanced usage docs example)
source_issues.evidence: Bug reproduced using the official advanced usage docs pattern. Root cause identified: append_messages sets _messages_modified=True, skipping auto-append of assistant+tool result. Infinite loop confirmed. The 'Modifying tool results' example on the same docs page uses a different correct pattern (appends both message and tool_response together).

signals.topic: Ambiguous 'Usage Limit' error messages — users cannot distinguish between limit types or take action
signals.summary: Claude surfaces different independent usage limits (session daily budget, weekly all-models budget, weekly Sonnet budget, API rate limits) but labels all identically as 'Usage Limit'. Users cannot determine which limit was hit, when it resets, or what to do next. Developers are forced to reverse-engineer limit types from context clues, preventing programmatic handling and meaningful user-facing guidance.
signals.review_reason: Significant developer experience degradation — all limit types return the same generic message, making it impossible to programmatically determine which limit was hit, when it resets, or what action to take. Prevents building meaningful user-facing error guidance. P2 due to count=1 and non-blocking nature (requests still execute, just fail after hitting a limit).

source_issues.title: [Enhancement] Standardize usage limit labels — replace ambiguous 'Usage Limit' with specific limit type identifiers
source_issues.evidence: All limit types (session budget, weekly budgets, API rate limits) return the same generic 'You've reached your usage limit. Please try again later.' message with no reset time and no actionable guidance. Developers building on the API cannot programmatically distinguish limit types.

signals.topic: TypeScript 类型定义错误：ContentBlock 类型无法直接访问 text 属性
signals.summary: 用户在升级 SDK 版本后，TypeScript 编译器报错 `Property 'text' does not exist on type 'ContentBlock'`，导致无法正常访问消息内容。被迫使用 `// @ts-ignore` 等变通方案，破坏类型安全。
aliases: TypeScript type error on ContentBlock.text property
signals.review_reason: 这是真实的用户痛点：TypeScript 类型定义导致用户主流程（读取消息内容）无法通过类型检查，被迫使用 `// @ts-ignore` 变通，实质上破坏了类型安全这一核心开发体验。9 条评论说明有多人受影响或关注。count=1 未达 P0 阈值，但影响明确，故列为 P1。

source_issues.title: [Types] Error: Property 'text' does not exist on type 'ContentBlock'.
source_issues.evidence: 用户在升级 v0.22.0 后无法访问 msg.content[0].text，TypeScript 报类型错误，被迫添加 `// @ts-ignore` 绕过，代码运行正常但失去类型安全。

signals.topic: Bundled Claude CLI hangs indefinitely when stdout is not a TTY, blocking all non-interactive deployments
signals.summary: The bundled Claude binary performs an isatty() check on stdout and switches behavior, causing Python SDK processes to hang silently when stdout is a pipe, file, Docker (no -t), CI runner, or cron/launchd job. No output, no error, no progress — only a hard timeout terminates the process.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary flow blocker: the SDK is completely unusable in any non-interactive environment (CI/CD, Docker, cron, headless servers). The repro is 100% reproducible and the bug silently consumes timeouts without diagnostic output, making it extremely hard to diagnose. Real production pipelines were blocked for 24+ hours.

source_issues.title: Bundled `claude` binary hangs when stdout is not a TTY (pipe / file / launchd / cron / Docker)
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro shows python script hangs indefinitely on pipe/file redirect but completes in 2s with TTY. A production launchd nightly pipeline timed out at 1800s every tick for 24+ hours due to this bug.

signals.topic: Autocompact thrashing when processing large files or tool outputs, preventing agent completion
signals.summary: When reading large files or processing large tool outputs, the context window hits its limit immediately after an autocompact operation, triggering a repeating thrash loop. The agent cannot complete its task.
signals.review_reason: Direct main workflow blocker: the agent cannot complete any task involving large files or outputs. The thrashing message explicitly tells the user the agent is stuck, which is a critical failure of the core agent loop.

source_issues.title: Bug: Autocompact is thrashing due to rapid context refill
source_issues.evidence: The agent encounters the error 'Autocompact is thrashing: the context refilled to the limit within 3 turns of the previous compact, 3 times in a row.' Reproduced with 64 skills, 6 subagents. The agent cannot make progress — the main workflow is blocked.

signals.topic: MCP server subprocesses leak after query() close, causing OOM and file-descriptor exhaustion in long-running processes
signals.summary: Query.close() only terminates the CLI parent process but never cleans up its child MCP server processes. These reparent to PID 1 and accumulate, leading to memory exhaustion, file-descriptor exhaustion, and CPU burn from polling MCP servers.
signals.review_reason: This is a cost/resource issue with clear evidence: each query() call leaks one MCP subprocess per configured server. Over hours of production use, the host OOMs — a measurable cost loss and service availability impact. The repro is deterministic and the root cause is confirmed in SDK source code.

source_issues.title: Query.close() does not reap MCP subprocess grandchildren
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer script proves PIDs of MCP sleep processes are reparented to PID 1 after Query.close(). The issue explicitly states OOM and file-descriptor exhaustion occur in long-running multi-call Python processes hosting the SDK.

signals.topic: TRACEPARENT trace context silently dropped on 2nd+ query() call in long-running server processes
signals.summary: On the first query() call the bundled CLI correctly nests its spans under the caller's W3C TRACEPARENT. On all subsequent calls in the same process lifetime, the same valid TRACEPARENT is silently ignored and spans become orphan roots. The trigger is ~/.claude/ state from prior runs.
signals.review_reason: Makes observability unreliable for the primary SDK deployment pattern (long-running server/worker processes), which is the documented recommended hosting model. Spans become uninterpretable after the first call, undermining monitoring and debugging capabilities. P1 rather than P0 because a workaround exists (override HOME per call).

source_issues.title: Bundled CLI silently drops inbound TRACEPARENT on 2nd+ query() call when ~/.claude/ has state from a prior run
source_issues.evidence: Python repro script with OpenTelemetry confirms call-1 spans nest correctly under TRACEPARENT; call-2+ spans emit with fresh trace IDs and no parent. Wiping ~/.claude/ restores correct behavior. This directly breaks the observability flow documented in the SDK hosting docs for the dominant server deployment shape.

signals.topic: TaskNotificationMessage fires prematurely while subagent is still executing tool calls, causing cascade workflow failures
signals.summary: When an orchestrator dispatches multiple subagents in parallel via the Task tool, the SDK occasionally delivers TaskNotificationMessage before the subagent has finished. The orchestrator receives a 'completion' signal while the subagent is still mid-execution (76-850 seconds remaining), leading to downstream agents dispatched against non-existent files and wasted compute.
signals.review_reason: Causes significant cascade failures in the SDK's own orchestration use case — the primary intended application. Wasted compute ($0.82 per run) and wrong outputs from downstream agents dispatched against non-existent state. The non-deterministic nature makes it particularly insidious. Downgraded from P0 only because count=1 and it's non-deterministic.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Orchestrator pattern 'subagent-X completes → dispatch reviewer-X' caused reviewers to be dispatched against non-existent files. 5 original researchers were re-dispatched (~8 min wasted). Actual run cost $21.51 with bug vs $22.33 baseline. Subagent was still at tool=13/39 when completion notification arrived. Timeline evidence with screenshots provided.

signals.topic: Isolation options (mcpServers: {}, settingSources: [], skills: []) fail to strip operator's claude.ai connector inventory from system init, causing context bloat and compacted_lost_tool_use escalation
signals.summary: When host programs pass documented isolation flags, the SDK's system init still ships the operator's full claude.ai connector inventory (88–370 mcp__claude_ai_* tools), agents, skills, and memory_paths.auto. This bloats the prompt by ~200–400KB and causes context window pressure that triggers premature response compaction, breaking bounded sub-agent workflows.
aliases: isolation flags not stripping claude.ai connector inventory
context bloat from operator tool bleed
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: host programs that explicitly opt into isolation via documented flags still get operator context bleeding into their SDK init, which directly causes main workflow failures (premature response compaction, tool_use blocks lost) and significant context window cost overhead. The evidence includes concrete numbers (88–370 tools, 200–400KB bloat) and a specific escalation reason (compacted_lost_tool_use). Count=1 but P1 due to clear non-trivial user impact.

source_issues.title: Options { mcpServers: {}, settingSources: [], skills: [] } doesn't strip claude.ai-connector tools, agents, or memory_paths.auto from system init (0.2.126)
source_issues.evidence: Host program explicitly passes mcpServers: {}, settingSources: [], skills: [] to achieve bounded-call isolation; init payload still contains 88–370 mcp__claude_ai_* tools, 6 agents, 8 skills, and populated memory_paths.auto. Prompt bloat is 200–400KB. Claude Sonnet 4.6 observed compacting responses before emitting tool_use blocks, causing compacted_lost_tool_use escalation on bounded calls that should have been within budget.

signals.topic: OTel tracer emits non-semconv token attribute names, causing downstream billing systems (e.g. Langfuse) to report $0 cost for all generations
signals.summary: The SDK's bundled OTel tracer uses bare attribute names (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens) instead of OTel GenAI semantic convention names. Downstream observability platforms that auto-extract cost from GenAI semconv attributes receive no token information and price every generation at $0, breaking cost tracking.
aliases: semantic convention violation in OTel tracing
token usage not extracted by downstream observability tools
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: downstream billing/observability systems fail to extract token usage data, resulting in every generation being priced at $0. This is a clear cost-tracking failure with concrete downstream impact. The evidence shows Langfuse's usage_details extraction fails systematically, not intermittently. Count=1 but P1 due to systematic billing anomaly.

source_issues.title: Tracer emits non-semconv token attributes (scope com.anthropic.claude_code.tracing v1.0.0) — continuation of #304 with new evidence
source_issues.evidence: Spans under scope com.anthropic.claude_code.tracing show usage_details: {} and calculated_total_cost: 0.0 in Langfuse because Langfuse maps from GenAI semconv attribute names but the SDK emits bare names (input_tokens vs gen_ai.usage.input_tokens). This is a persistent billing anomaly — every generation is priced at $0, not a one-off.

signals.topic: Native Bun binary distribution (~230 MB) exceeds Vercel/AWS Lambda serverless deployment limits (250 MB), rendering SDK unusable in serverless environments
signals.summary: Since version 0.2.110, the SDK ships a ~230 MB Bun-compiled native binary via optionalDependencies. This exceeds Vercel's 250 MB function size cap and is too close to AWS Lambda's limit, blocking serverless deployments. No JS-only distribution alternative exists.
aliases: serverless deployment blocked by binary size
230 MB Bun binary exceeds Vercel function size limit
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine P0 user pain point: an entire major deployment target (serverless/Vercel/Lambda) is completely blocked. The binary exceeds the hard limit by ~8% with zero wiggle room for application code. The user cannot downgrade to a working version because the skills API needed for their use case was only introduced after the switch to native distribution. No viable workaround exists.

source_issues.title: Native binary distribution (≥0.2.110) makes Agent SDK unusable in Vercel/Lambda serverless deployments (230 MB pushes past the 250 MB function size cap)
source_issues.evidence: Deploying a minimal Next.js app importing @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk to Vercel fails with 'Native CLI binary for linux-x64 not found'. Attempting outputFileTracingIncludes to bundle the binary fails the 250 MB function size check — the binary alone is 230 MB. No JS-only fallback exists because the skills API was implemented after the last JS-bundled version (0.2.109) which lacks the skills field.

signals.topic: createSdkMcpServer strips Zod v4 .describe() from nested properties and tools registered via registerTool after initialization
signals.summary: The fix in #243 backfills Zod field descriptions only for flat top-level shape values during createSdkMcpServer call. Nested properties' .describe() annotations and tools added via registerTool() after initialization are both dropped, resulting in AI agents seeing incomplete or missing tool descriptions.
aliases: Zod describe not backfilled for nested properties
tool description stripped from MCP server schemas
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: tool descriptions are silently dropped for nested Zod properties and post-init registered tools, causing AI agents to receive incomplete tool schemas. However, count=1 and it does not block a major deployment target or cause billing anomalies — it's an edge-case DX degradation. P2 appropriate.

source_issues.title: createSdkMcpServer drops Zod v4 field .describe() if nested or added after via registerTool
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro shows z.string().describe('This description is dropped') on a nested property is not backfilled. Similarly, registerTool() called after createSdkMcpServer() loses field descriptions. Root cause is a flat loop with no recursion in the backfill logic. Labels: bug.

signals.topic: restoreConfigFromBase crashes on symlinks — ENOENT on dangling symlinks or symlinks outside SENSITIVE_PATTS (v1 regression from May 14)
signals.summary: The `restoreConfigFromBase` step in v1 crashes with `ENOENT` when `.claude/` contains symlinks. Two variants: (a) dangling symlinks whose targets don't exist yet, and (b) valid symlinks whose resolved target lies outside the SENSITIVE_PATHS set. Regression introduced 2026-05-14 by dereference:true change + Bun 1.3.14 bump. All PR workflows in affected repos are blocked.
aliases: dangling symlink crash in restore step
signals.review_reason: count=3 with confirmed regression timeline (last green May 14 18:02 UTC, first red May 15 13:28 UTC). Root cause is a compound regression from two merged PRs on May 14. All PR workflows in affected repos are completely blocked — this is a primary-path failure. P0 is warranted due to count>=3, CI-pathway blocking, and explicit reproduction evidence.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase ENOENT on .claude/ symlinks whose target is outside SENSITIVE_PATHS
source_issues.evidence: cpSync with dereference:true + Bun 1.3.14 causes ENOENT on valid symlinks pointing outside SENSITIVE_PATHS. Every PR in affected repo has failed since 2026-05-15. Confirmed last-green vs first-red timeline. Workaround: pin to SHA 86eb26bf.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase crashes on dangling symlinks in .claude/ directory
source_issues.evidence: restoreConfigFromBase fails with ENOENT when .claude/skills/ contains symlinks whose targets don't exist at action runtime. Regression from v2.1.142. Workflow fails at restore step, blocking all PR reviews.

source_issues.title: v1 tag recently crashing
source_issues.evidence: v1 tag crashes with 'directory mismatch' errors in CI. Same root cause as #1319/#1321 — symlink handling regression. Issue explicitly states 'did not happen before, has the tag recently moved?'

signals.topic: Workflow validation fails when base branch name contains '#' character
signals.summary: When a repository's default branch name contains a '#' character (e.g., feat/#689-v1.2.0), the action skips execution with 'workflow validation failed'. The '#' is likely interpreted as a YAML comment delimiter in the action's branch-name comparison logic.
aliases: branch name with hash breaks action
yaml comment char in branch name validation
signals.review_reason: Single-repository count, but root cause is a clear bug in the action's branch-name comparison logic — '#' being treated as a YAML comment delimiter causes the action to silently skip. Any repo with a '#' in its default branch name is completely broken. While count=1, the impact is non-trivial and the fix is likely a one-liner (shell quoting). P1 is appropriate as it is a non-blocking but impactful workflow failure for affected repos.

source_issues.title: workflow validation failed if base branch's name has # in it
source_issues.evidence: Changing default branch name to include '#' (e.g., feat/#689-v1.2.0) causes action to skip with 'workflow validation failed'. Renaming branch to 'develop/v1.2.0' fixes it immediately with no workflow changes.

signals.topic: GitHub App bot comments (github-actions[bot]) do not trigger @claude workflow — only subsequent user comments do, causing duplicate runs
signals.summary: When a GitHub Actions bot (github-actions[bot]) posts a PR comment mentioning @claude, the action marks the comment but does not trigger. A follow-up user comment triggers the workflow twice — once for the bot comment and once for the user comment. This causes duplicate Claude invocations and wasted API quota.
aliases: bot comment @claude does not trigger action
duplicate Claude invocation from bot comments
signals.review_reason: Long-standing bug (open since Sep 2025, 17 comments) affecting bot-driven workflows. The bot comment silently fails to trigger while consuming Claude's attention (👀 reaction), and the subsequent user comment causes duplicate invocations — wasting API quota and potentially posting duplicate reviews. While count=1, the pattern is well-documented and clearly reproducible.

source_issues.title: Github Bot PR comment doesn't trigger Claude even though invoked
source_issues.evidence: When github-actions bot comments '@claude solve this ticket', Claude marks it with 👀 but doesn't trigger the workflow. A follow-up '@claude solve this ticket' from a human triggers the workflow twice (once per comment). Active issue since Sep 2025 with 17 comments and no resolution.

signals.topic: OAuth token (sk-ant-oat01-*) fails with 'Header 14 invalid value' in GitHub Actions despite working locally
signals.summary: Users on Max 5x plan using `claude_code_oauth_token` with tokens from `claude setup-token` (prefix sk-ant-oat01-*) get 'API Error: Header 14 has invalid value' during SDK execution in the GitHub Actions runner, even though the same token works locally with `claude -p`.
aliases: claude setup-token oauth token header error in CI
sk-ant-oat01 token invalid in GitHub Actions
signals.review_reason: OAuth token flow broken in GitHub Actions for Max 5x users despite working locally. Count=1, but blocks a specific auth path (OAuth tokens in CI). The failure is after OIDC/app-token exchange — specifically at the Claude Code SDK call — indicating a token format incompatibility between the action's SDK invocation and the OAuth token format. P2 given single-reporter count but the issue is well-scoped and actionable.

source_issues.title: claude_code_oauth_token (sk-ant-oat01-*) fails with Header 14 invalid value
source_issues.evidence: OAuth token generated by 'claude setup-token' (Max 5x plan, sk-ant-oat01-*) fails with 'Header 14 invalid value' during SDK execution. OIDC and app token exchange succeed, but SDK fails. Same token works locally with 'claude -p'. Action version: v1 SHA 51ea8ea.

signals.topic: GitHub connector/integration failures blocking repo access across web, desktop, and CLI surfaces
signals.summary: GitHub repos are not visible or accessible in Claude Code despite the Claude GitHub App being correctly installed. This affects three distinct surfaces: (1) claude.ai/code web repo picker shows 'No repos match' despite app installed with all-repos access; (2) desktop app Cowork GitHub browsing shows connector as 'connected' but no auth prompt appears and repos cannot be browsed; (3) /autofix-pr CLI command fails with 'Claude GitHub app must be installed' despite correct installation. All traced to a known backend repository index failure.
aliases: GitHub app not recognized by backend
signals.review_reason: GitHub integration is a core product feature across multiple surfaces. The web repo picker failure blocks users from starting Claude Code sessions from GitHub repos. The /autofix-pr failure blocks automated PR fixing — a key productivity feature. Both are distinct primary workflows being blocked. Affects Windows, WSL, and web users. Root cause is the same known backend repository index failure, but user-facing symptoms are distinct across surfaces.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Github connector not working on desktop app or web
source_issues.evidence: GitHub connector shows as 'connected' but no auth prompt appears on connect attempt. Affects both desktop app and web interface on Windows. User checked with admin account — all settings are correct and active. Cowork feature cannot be used to browse GitHub repositories.

source_issues.title: [BUG] /autofix-pr fails with 'Claude GitHub app must be installed' despite app being installed
source_issues.evidence: /autofix-pr fails with 'The Claude GitHub app must be installed on this repository first' error even though the app is correctly installed and configured with access to the repository. References known backend indexing issue from #21377 and #30872. Uninstall/reinstall workaround did not resolve it.

signals.topic: Read tool returns stale cached content after external on-disk edits, causing incorrect code generation
signals.summary: The Read tool caches file contents and suppresses re-reads with a 'Wasted call — file unchanged' message. The freshness check only tracks edits made by Claude's own tools (Edit, Write, NotebookEdit), ignoring external disk modifications. When a file is edited externally (another terminal, IDE save, another process, git pull), the Read tool still returns the stale cached snapshot. This causes Claude to operate on outdated information and make incorrect code changes.
aliases: Read tool ignores external file changes
Read tool serves outdated content after external edits
signals.review_reason: Real workflow blocker. Read is a core primary tool; serving stale cached content causes Claude to reason on wrong context and produce incorrect code changes. Has reproducible steps (4-step repro provided). Workaround (Bash cat) exists but defeats the purpose of the Read tool and requires user intervention. Blocks the main coding workflow.

source_issues.title: [BUG] `Read` tool returns 'file unchanged' after external on-disk edits, serving a stale cached snapshot
source_issues.evidence: Read tool suppresses re-reads with 'Wasted call — file unchanged' message, tracking only internal edits (Edit/Write/NotebookEdit) not external disk modifications. User confirmed: edits made in VSCode notebook editor between two Read calls are not detected. Assistant runs `cat | jq` via Bash to recover actual content, confirming Read was wrong. Inconsistent with Edit tool which performs real disk-state check per documented behavior. No workaround within the Read tool itself — requires Bash workaround.

signals.topic: /usage statistics persist from old account after account switch via /login
signals.summary: After a user switches their Claude Code account using the /login command in the same filesystem context, the /usage command continues to display historical usage statistics from the previous account instead of the newly authenticated one.
aliases: usage command stale data after login switch
signals.review_reason: Real auth/session state bug. Shows misleading billing and usage data after account switch, which can cause users to make incorrect decisions about their account usage and billing. Affects users who share machines or switch between personal/enterprise accounts. Non-blocking but clearly incorrect behavior with a clear repro path.

source_issues.title: [BUG] /usage statistics keep old account stats when you change accounts
source_issues.evidence: User switched from personal to enterprise account via /login in the same Claude Code filesystem. The /usage command then showed usage data from two months ago (personal account usage) instead of enterprise account stats, even though enterprise sessions (133 sessions) were running. Stats should reflect the currently logged-in account only.

signals.topic: Read tool documentation describes obsolete error behavior instead of current partial-content fallback
signals.summary: The official Read tool documentation still describes the pre-v2.1.145 behavior where oversized whole-file reads return a hard error. Since v2.1.145, the Read tool actually returns a truncated first page labeled 'PARTIAL view' instead of failing, and the docs omit this fallback behavior entirely.
signals.review_reason: Documentation bug describing wrong tool behavior. Users who consult docs expecting a hard error on oversized reads will be confused when Claude silently returns partial content instead. This leads to unexpected Claude behavior and potential missed context in large-file operations. Impact is user-facing confusion rather than workflow blockage, hence P2.

source_issues.title: [DOCS] Read tool docs still describe oversized whole-file reads as hard errors
source_issues.evidence: Docs state 'Files over a size threshold return an error rather than partial content, prompting Claude to retry with offset and limit'. As of v2.1.145, Read returns truncated content labeled 'PARTIAL view' instead of hard-failing. Docs omit the new fallback behavior and the PARTIAL view notice. Users relying on docs will have incorrect expectations about tool behavior.

signals.topic: Stop and SubagentStop hook documentation omits newly added background_tasks and session_crons input fields
signals.summary: The Claude Code v2.1.145 changelog announced that Stop and SubagentStop hooks now receive background_tasks and session_crons input fields, but the official hooks documentation page, Agent SDK TypeScript docs, and Python docs all still list only the old field sets. Hook authors cannot discover or use these new fields.
signals.review_reason: Documentation bug omitting newly added API fields from v2.1.145. Hook authors relying on official docs will not know that background_tasks and session_crons fields are available in Stop/SubagentStop hooks. This prevents feature adoption and correct hook implementations. Multiple documentation surfaces are affected (main hooks docs + TypeScript SDK + Python SDK). Impact is blocked feature discovery rather than workflow blockage, hence P2.

source_issues.title: [DOCS] Stop and SubagentStop hook input docs omit `background_tasks` and `session_crons`
source_issues.evidence: Changelog for v2.1.145 announced Stop and SubagentStop hooks now include 'background_tasks' and 'session_crons' fields. The main hooks docs page (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) still shows only the old field lists. Agent SDK TypeScript (code-site) and Python docs also omit these fields from StopHookInput and SubagentStopHookInput definitions. Hook authors cannot discover these new fields, preventing them from building functionality around background tasks and session crons.

signals.topic: Summarization cookbook fails with BadRequestError due to deprecated assistant message prefill
signals.summary: The `capabilities/summarization/guide.ipynb` notebook is broken because it uses assistant message prefill, which has been deprecated. Cell 8 throws a BadRequestError with 'This model does not support assistant message prefill', making the cookbook unusable for users who run through it.
signals.review_reason: 用户实际运行 cookbook 时主流程被 BadRequestError 阻断，属于关键示例不可用。虽然 count=1，但提供了完整的复现步骤和错误堆栈，证据充分；降级为 P1 是因为单仓单 issue 不满足 P0 的高频要求。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Summarization cookbook fails due to use of assistant message prefill
source_issues.evidence: Cell 8 in the summarization cookbook throws BadRequestError: 'This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.' The notebook is completely broken and cannot be run end-to-end.

signals.topic: hookify plugin crashes on Python 3.8 and Korean Windows (cp949) — all hooks silently fail
signals.summary: hookify plugin uses PEP 585 generics (tuple[...] syntax) evaluated at import time, causing TypeError on Python <3.9. Also opens files without explicit UTF-8 encoding, causing UnicodeDecodeError on cp949-locale Windows. Both bugs block all hook functionality (block/warn rules, Stop/PostToolUse hooks).
signals.review_reason: Two independent bugs in the same plugin both result in ALL hookify hooks (block, warn, Stop, PostToolUse) being completely non-functional. Users on Python 3.8 (common macOS default) and Korean Windows (cp949 locale) cannot use any hookify rules. The Python 3.8 crash is a module-level import failure, the cp949 issue silently returns empty dict for every rule evaluation.

source_issues.title: hookify: config_loader.py crashes on Python 3.8 — uses PEP 585 generics without future import or version pin
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: 'type' object is not subscriptable at import time. Prevents ALL hookify hooks (Stop, PostToolUse, etc.) from running on any Python 3.8 system (common on macOS). Workaround requires manual Python upgrade.

source_issues.title: hookify: UTF-8 encoding fix needed for Korean Windows (cp949)
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp949' codec can't decode byte 0xf0 on every rule file. load_rule_file() catches and returns None — block/warn rules silently drop. Reproduced on Windows 11 Korean locale, Python 3.12.

signals.topic: Plugin submissions show 'Published' in dashboard but are not installable — missing from marketplace.json
signals.summary: Two community plugin submissions (Claude Code Inspect, llm-dark-patterns) show 'Published' status in claude.ai plugin submissions dashboard but do not appear in the community marketplace.json. Users cannot install via 'claude plugin install <name>@claude-community'. Root cause: submissions pipeline does not sync published plugins to marketplace.json.
signals.review_reason: Plugin submissions are published in the dashboard but never actually sync to marketplace.json, making them completely un-installable. Two independent users have reported this for two different plugins, with #1887 explicitly linking back to #1272 as a recurrence of the same pipeline bug. This is a systemic submission pipeline failure that wastes developer effort and leaves published plugins in a limbo state.

source_issues.title: My submission published but i can't find it anywhere?!
source_issues.evidence: Plugin 'Claude Code Inspect' shows 'Published' on dashboard but is not findable in the Claude Code plugin marketplace. User can only see it via direct URL to their submission screenshot.

source_issues.title: Submission published but not appearing in marketplace.json: llm-dark-patterns (follow-up to #1272)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed via curl against marketplace.json (1715 entries): zero matches for 'waitdeadai' org or 'llm-dark-patterns' name. jq verification provided. Issue reopened with fresh evidence after #1272 was closed without resolution. Both 'Claude Code Inspect' and 'llm-dark-patterns' show 'Published' but are not in marketplace.json.

signals.topic: ralph-loop stop-hook crashes with empty stderr on every session end for markdown-only state files
signals.summary: ralph-loop stop-hook.sh uses set -e; when the state file has no YAML frontmatter, grep exits 1 and aborts before any error output. User sees 'Stop hook error: Failed with non-blocking status code: No stderr output' with no actionable signal. The pr-review-loop skill (and similar) deliberately writes markdown-only state files.
signals.review_reason: ralph-loop stop hook crashes on every single Claude Code session end for any user of the pr-review-loop skill or any skill using markdown-only state files. The error message is uninterpretable ('No stderr output'). This is a main-flow event (session end) being disrupted every time, producing noise in every affected session.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop stop-hook exits 1 with empty stderr when .claude/ralph-loop.local.md lacks YAML frontmatter
source_issues.evidence: set -e aborts hook before error output on every session end. Affects any project using the pr-review-loop skill (and similar) that writes .claude/ralph-loop.local.md as markdown-only. Full repro script provided. tracecore skill already renamed its state file as a workaround.

signals.topic: Slack Connector OAuth fails on Slack Enterprise Grid — no_bot_scopes_requested error blocks reconnection
signals.summary: Slack Enterprise Grid workspace migration (2026-05-02) broke the Slack Connector OAuth flow. Reconnect returns no_bot_scopes_requested from Slack's oauth/v2_user/authorize endpoint. Previously issued tokens invalidated, all downstream automations fail with invalid_auth_token.
signals.review_reason: Slack Connector is completely non-functional for Slack Enterprise Grid users after a migration. All existing tokens invalidated, OAuth cannot complete, all downstream automations fail. This is a total feature outage for the affected org type. The workaround (manual copy-paste) is a significant regression from the connector-based workflow.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin bun subprocess survives Claude Code exit, causing 409 conflict and 99% CPU spin on reconnection
signals.summary: Two bugs: (1) onStart resets the 409-exit counter to 0, making the retry loop never exit; (2) .in_use/ PID markers leak on ungraceful exit, and bun server.ts survives its parent. Competing bun processes fight over the same bot token, causing 409 on every poll cycle, with one process burning 99% CPU indefinitely.
signals.review_reason: Telegram plugin bun subprocess survives Claude Code exit, creating a token conflict that prevents any Telegram connection from succeeding. One process burns a full CPU core at 99%, causing real CPU throttling on the host machine. The user had to kill the process manually with SIGKILL. This is both a resource exhaustion and a complete plugin failure.

SIGTERM ignored, SIGKILL required. Competing bun processes with 409 Conflict on every poll. Verified on macOS Intel i7-9750H.

signals.topic: README states Python 3.8+ but code requires Python 3.10+ causing immediate TypeError on import
signals.summary: The agents/README.md advertises Python 3.8+ as the minimum requirement, yet the source code uses PEP 604 union syntax (X | None) and PEP 585 generics (list[...]) in runtime-evaluated annotations that require Python 3.10+. Users following the README and running on Python 3.8/3.9 hit a TypeError immediately on `from agents.agent import Agent`, blocking the main flow from the first step.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it causes main-flow failure: users who follow the documented requirements and install on Python 3.8 or 3.9 immediately encounter a TypeError when importing the agent module, blocking all further usage. The discrepancy between documented requirement (3.8+) and actual requirement (3.10+) is clearly demonstrated with concrete code examples in the issue body.

signals.topic: pptx skill produces .pptx files that fail to import into Apple Keynote (OOXML compliance issues)
signals.summary: The pptx skill generates .pptx files that Apple Keynote refuses to import on macOS, due to three silent OOXML compliance violations: contradictory `<p:sldSz>` type attribute with widescreen dimensions, missing `<p:notesMasterIdLst>` in presentation.xml, and embedded Windows-only printer settings stub. Files work in PowerPoint/Online/LibreOffice but fail silently in Keynote with no diagnostic. Workaround requires OneDrive round-trip.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: the main deliverable (a .pptx file) is broken for a significant subset of users (macOS Keynote users). The failure is silent (no error message until the user tries to open the file) and forces users to either install PowerPoint or perform a manual OneDrive round-trip as workaround. The issue has detailed root cause analysis and a reproducible test case, confirming genuine user impact on the primary output of the pptx skill.

source_issues.evidence: Files produced by python-pptx via the pptx skill cannot be imported into Apple Keynote on macOS. User-visible error: 'Das Dateiformat ist ungültig' / 'The file format is invalid'. Quick Look also fails. PowerPoint Online sanitizes the file on round-trip, confirming the issue is in the skill's output. Estimated impact: 'significant fraction of macOS users in Cowork mode hit this with no recourse other than installing PowerPoint.' Three root causes identified and documented with exact OOXML patches.

signals.topic: Skills referencing platform-unavailable tools fail silently with no error signal to users or authors
signals.summary: When a SKILL.md references a tool that doesn't exist on the running platform, Claude silently falls back to prose output or substitutes a different tool with incompatible semantics. No error is surfaced. For example, Claude Code's `Write` is silently substituted with Claude.ai's `create_file` which has opposite overwrite semantics. Six of seven Claude.ai-only tools tested produced no error on Claude Code. Skills work 'correctly' on one platform but silently degrade or produce opposite behavior on another.
signals.review_reason: This is a high-impact P0 pain point: skills silently produce wrong or opposite behavior (Write vs create_file have opposite overwrite semantics) with NO error signal to either the user or the skill author. The cross-platform tool substitution issue means a skill can be 'correct' on the development platform and broken on the target platform without any indication. This directly defeats the purpose of skills — the core product value. Six of seven Claude.ai-only tools fail silently. The opposite-semantics example (Write vs create_file) is a concrete, high-severity user impact.

source_issues.title: Skills referencing tools that don't exist on the running platform fail silently
source_issues.evidence: Reproductions documented: (A) Claude.ai tools like `ask_user_input_v0`, `image_search`, `conversation_search` produce no error on Claude Code — Claude silently falls back to prose. (B) Claude Code tools like `Write` are silently substituted with `create_file` on Claude.ai, which has OPPOSITE overwrite semantics (Write overwrites; create_file refuses with 'File already exists'). Skills behave differently on each platform with zero user/author signal. The issue explicitly states: 'skill author has no signal until a user reports a confusing failure.' Cross-platform skill development is 'effectively untestable from one platform.'

signals.topic: references/ relative paths do not resolve from skill directory — core functionality broken
signals.summary: The `skill-creator` skill recommends the `references/` progressive-disclosure pattern, but neither Claude.ai's `view` nor Claude Code's `Read` resolves relative paths from the skill's own directory. Paths are resolved against the process cwd instead. On Claude.ai, relative paths are rejected outright ('not an absolute path'). Skills wanting to load their own `references/` files cannot do so, requiring workarounds that are not documented in skill-creator.
signals.review_reason: This directly breaks a first-party recommended pattern (references/ progressive disclosure) from the official skill-creator skill. The functionality is entirely non-working: paths resolve to the wrong directory (cwd), and on Claude.ai they are outright rejected. This affects any skill author following the official documentation and represents a fundamental gap between documented behavior and actual behavior. Skill authors following the recommended pattern will encounter silent failures.

signals.topic: skill-creator run_loop.py crashes without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY during improve step — main iteration loop blocked
signals.summary: The skill-creator's run_loop.py crashes during the 'Improving description...' step (scripts/improve_description.py) with a TypeError about missing authentication, because it constructs `anthropic.Anthropic()` directly instead of using `claude -p` subprocess like the eval step. Users with only a Claude/Claude Code subscription (no API key) can complete iteration 1 but cannot proceed past it. The skill's own SKILL.md implies the entire flow should work via subscription.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking issue: the main iteration loop of the official skill-creator tool crashes after the first iteration, preventing users without API keys from using the core improvement workflow. The crash occurs mid-pipeline with no recovery path. The inconsistency between eval (works) and improve (crashes) steps creates a broken experience that contradicts the skill's own documentation implying subscription-based auth throughout.

This is a core UX regression that breaks the built-in Autovisualiser and Apps extensions, making a primary feature of the product completely unusable in embedded mode. Both v1.34.0 and v1.34.1 affected, with workaround (new window) confirmed but embedded mode broken.

signals.topic: Anthropic provider returns 400 error when using parameterless MCP tools in multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: When an Anthropic provider conversation includes a tool call to a parameterless MCP tool (one whose schema declares no input properties), Goose stores the tool_use block with null input. On the next conversation turn, when Goose replays the conversation history to the API, it serializes the null input as JSON null instead of {}, causing Anthropic to reject the request with 'messages.<N>.content.<M>.tool_use.input: Input should be an object'. The first tool call succeeds but any follow-up immediately fails with 400. This is a known pattern already fixed for Bedrock (#8121) but not applied to the Anthropic provider.
aliases: parameterless MCP tool Anthropic multi-turn failure
signals.review_reason: API-level blocking bug: Anthropic provider returns HTTP 400 for any conversation that previously used a parameterless MCP tool. Root cause precisely identified (null vs {} serialization), known fix pattern from Bedrock regression, no user workaround. Any multi-turn conversation with a parameterless MCP tool is permanently broken — the only resolution is starting a new session. Given the technical clarity of the root cause and the complete absence of a workaround, this meets P0 despite count=1. The bug is in the core Anthropic provider path and affects all Anthropic users with common MCP server patterns.

source_issues.title: Error using a parameterless MCP tool with Anthropic provider
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in crates/goose/src/providers/formats/anthropic.rs:174. Serializes tool_call.arguments (None) as JSON null instead of {}. Fails with 400 on the message immediately after the first parameterless tool call. Same bug pattern fixed for Bedrock in #8121. No workaround — users must avoid parameterless MCP tools or start new sessions. Widely-used MCP servers expose parameterless tools (list_things, file system introspection).

signals.topic: preserve_thinking_context flag is ineffective for all OpenAI-compatible providers — thinking content silently stripped from conversation history
signals.summary: The preserve_thinking_context flag does not work for any OpenAI-compatible provider (omlx, lmstudio, llama_swap, OpenAI-compatible endpoints). Thinking content is unconditionally filtered out by agent_visible_content() before messages reach the provider's format module, so reasoning_content is never emitted in API requests. Models that rely on receiving their own reasoning on subsequent turns get empty context, degrading multi-turn reasoning quality.
aliases: thinking context stripped for lmstudio llmstudio llama_swap
signals.review_reason: preserve_thinking_context is a documented feature that is silently broken for all OpenAI-compatible providers. The flag is rendered completely ineffective — no error is thrown but the feature does not work. This directly degrades multi-turn reasoning quality for any user of lmstudio, ollama, OpenRouter with OpenAI-compatible endpoints, or similar providers. Root cause precisely located and fix identified.

source_issues.title: preserve_thinking_context ineffective for OpenAI-compatible providers
source_issues.evidence: Root cause in crates/goose/src/conversation/message.rs:380 — agent_visible_content() calls filter_for_audience(Role::Assistant) which unconditionally strips MessageContent::Thinking. Since filtering happens before the provider format module, reasoning_text is always empty for all OpenAI-compatible providers. 2 comments indicate active discussion. Fix proposed.

signals.topic: Telegram gateway GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS hardcoded to 5 — cannot be overridden, making Telegram unusable for multi-step automation
signals.summary: The Telegram gateway has GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS hardcoded to 5 in the Rust source (crates/goose/src/gateway/handler.rs:319). No configuration option (GOOSE_MAX_TURNS, config.yaml, gateway_configs, session settings) affects it. Telegram sessions stop after exactly 5 LLM turns with a prompt asking user to continue. When user replies 'Yes', extensions_changed=true triggers session restore and the bot starts over from step 1, hitting the limit again — creating an infinite loop. Any workflow requiring more than 5 tool calls is impossible to complete via Telegram.
aliases: Telegram cannot run workflows longer than 5 turns
Telegram session infinite loop after 5 turns
signals.review_reason: The Telegram gateway is effectively broken for any real-world multi-step workflow. The hardcoded limit of 5 turns combined with the session restore behavior creates an infinite loop, making the Telegram integration completely unusable for its intended purpose. User demonstrates this with concrete log evidence and exhaustively documents all failed workarounds. Although count=1, the severity (complete feature block) and clear root cause justify P1.

source_issues.title: Telegram gateway: GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS hardcoded to 5 — cannot be overridden by GOOSE_MAX_TURNS or any config
source_issues.evidence: Hardcoded GATEWAY_MAX_TURNS: u32 = 5 in crates/goose/src/gateway/handler.rs. Log evidence shows exactly 5 turns then stop. All configuration attempts fail (GOOSE_MAX_TURNS: 9999, recipe settings, gateway_configs). Replying 'Yes' triggers session restart → hits limit again → infinite loop. Makes Telegram completely unusable for any multi-step automation (browser automation + email OTP workflows).

signals.topic: Severe memory leak in Docker container when MCP tool returns very large responses (~3 million characters)
signals.summary: When goose-server runs inside a Docker container and an MCP tool returns very large responses (~3 million characters / ~3MB of text), RAM spikes sharply and never returns to baseline. Repeated calls cause continuous memory growth exceeding 10GB. Memory only recovers after restarting the entire Docker container. This issue does not occur on native macOS or Windows — it is specific to the Docker/Linux container environment. This caps the maximum output size users can process and causes production OOM failures in containerized deployments.
aliases: Docker memory not reclaimed after large tool response
OOM in Docker with large MCP tool output
signals.review_reason: Severe memory leak in Docker deployments causes unbounded RAM growth and eventual OOM when MCP tools return large outputs. Production-impacting: containers must be restarted to recover, making long-running Docker deployments unstable. Different behavior from native platforms indicates a container-specific memory management bug.

source_issues.title: Severe memory leak in Docker container when MCP tool returns very large responses (~3 million characters)

Not reproducible on native macOS/Windows — Linux container specific. Affects production goosed deployments using Docker.

source_issues.evidence: AWS GovCloud West model list shows legacy models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Haiku with end-of-life dates) and lacks current models. Users have no override option to use correct models. Government cloud users cannot access current AI models.

signals.topic: CLI process leak after task completion
signals.summary: CLI leaves orphaned cline.exe processes (245MB+ each) running after completing tasks, progressively exhausting system resources on repeated invocations.
signals.review_reason: Process leak is a confirmed resource exhaustion issue. Each CLI invocation leaks a ~245MB process that accumulates indefinitely. Main flow blocking for any user running multiple CLI tasks, progressively degrading system performance until failure.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 leaks running processes after handling a session task
source_issues.evidence: CLI leaves orphaned cline.exe processes running after completing tasks. Each invocation adds another leaked process (245MB+ RAM each) that never terminates. After a few tasks, system resources are significantly consumed.

signals.topic: CLI config command does not persist settings across invocations
signals.summary: Using 'cline config' TUI to modify settings appears to work in-session but all changes are lost upon exit. User must reconfigure every CLI invocation.
signals.review_reason: Complete failure of CLI config persistence — the primary purpose of a config command. User cannot establish persistent preferences, forcing manual reconfiguration on every invocation. Blocks the intended CLI usage pattern entirely.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 config does not persist configuration changes
source_issues.evidence: Using 'cline config' TUI to modify settings (e.g., switching from Act to Plan mode) appears to work in-session but all changes are lost upon exit. No global-settings.json is created. User must reconfigure every single CLI invocation.

signals.topic: CLI --json mode cannot resume existing session with --id flag
signals.summary: Using --json and --id together to resume a session fails with 'JSON output mode requires a prompt argument or piped stdin', blocking automation workflows.
signals.review_reason: Breaking the --json mode resume workflow blocks automation and scripted usage patterns. The incompatibility between --json and --id flags makes it impossible to programmatically continue conversations.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 --json mode can't resume an existing session ID
source_issues.evidence: Using --json and --id together to resume a session fails with 'JSON output mode requires a prompt argument or piped stdin'. This blocks the entire scripted/automation workflow for continuing conversations, a core use case for JSON mode.

signals.topic: Runtime ReferenceError 'Headers is not defined' causes LLM streaming to fail completely
signals.summary: The Continue VS Code extension references the Web standard `Headers` API in a Node.js / browser extension context where it is not available, causing a ReferenceError that prevents ALL LLM API requests from being sent. Requests never reach the server — this is a complete workflow blocker.
aliases: Headers API not available in extension context
signals.review_reason: P0 because the error fires at the buildHeaders call before any HTTP request is dispatched — no LLM interaction is possible at all. This is a main-flow blocker affecting VS Code and code-server environments with openai-compatible providers. Two distinct issues (#12163, #5079) and multiple affected users per issue body confirm this is not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: "Headers not defined" -> This time with logs
source_issues.evidence: ReferenceError: Headers is not defined at buildHeaders. A request is NEVER made to the web server. Confirmed across VS Code + code-server environments.

source_issues.title: 400 Error
source_issues.evidence: ReferenceError: Headers is not defined AND HTTP 400 from model-proxy. Log traces show the same buildHeaders failure. Issue is closed but root cause is unfixed.

signals.topic: Hard 16k token limit on read_file tool blocks Plan mode with large codebases
signals.summary: Continue enforces a 16384 token hard cap on the read_file tool. When a file exceeds this limit, read_file silently fails with a 'File is too large' error, making Plan mode unusable for any project with large files — a core use case is completely blocked.
signals.review_reason: P1 because while count=1, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: Plan mode (a core workflow) is completely blocked, the user's files cannot be fractioned, and there is no workaround. The token limit is documented as a hard-coded constant, affecting any non-trivial codebase. Not P0 only because single-incident evidence is insufficient for P0 classification.

source_issues.title: Size limit for Read_File
source_issues.evidence: User reports Plan mode fails entirely: 'read_file failed: File is too large (33450 tokens vs 16384 token limit)'. The hard 16k limit cannot be worked around for large files that cannot be split.

signals.topic: Continue Hub OAuth login silently fails, users cannot authenticate and are blocked from hub features
signals.summary: Users setting up Continue Hub authentication complete the OAuth flow but are redirected back to the login page with a 'Not authenticated (user missing)' error when accessing hub.continue.dev/inbox. Multiple browsers, clean profiles, and network variations all reproduce the issue, indicating a broken authentication callback or session establishment.
signals.review_reason: P1 — count=1 but review_reason provides exhaustive evidence of a complete auth flow failure: the user tried every possible workaround (clean profiles, different OAuth methods, revoked access, VPN variations) and all reproduce the same broken state. This blocks onboarding for new users entirely. Not P0 because single-incident evidence alone is insufficient for P0.

source_issues.title: Login failed with "Not authenticated (user missing)" after account setup
source_issues.evidence: User goes through full OAuth flow (GitHub + Google), sees 'Setting up your account...', then redirected to login page. Opening hub.continue.dev/inbox directly shows 'Not authenticated (user missing)'. Tried clean browser profiles, different auth methods, revoked OAuth access, VPN and non-VPN networks — all reproduce. Core onboarding flow is broken.

signals.topic: LocalAI streaming responses are not detected by Continue, resulting in zero-token empty responses
signals.summary: Continue cannot parse LocalAI's streaming response format (both v3.0.0 and v3.10.0). Despite the response chunks arriving over the network (confirmed via Wireshark), Continue never displays them and waits for the full stream to complete with 0 generated tokens. Users get completely empty responses from all LocalAI-hosted models.
signals.review_reason: P1 — count=1 but the evidence is extensive and unambiguous: Wireshark confirmation that data arrives, token logs showing 0 generated tokens, reproduction across two LocalAI versions and two OSes with multiple models. This is a functional integration failure (not a missing feature) where the core use case of chatting with a LocalAI model produces zero output. The breadth of reproduction conditions elevates confidence beyond single-issue noise.

source_issues.title: Responses from LLM's running from LocalAI are not detected
source_issues.evidence: Wireshark confirms streamed chunks arrive but Continue never displays them. Token log shows 'Generated Tokens: 0' despite 7.6s of streaming on a 421-token prompt. Reproduced on both LocalAI v3.0.0 and v3.10.0, across Windows and Linux, with multiple different GGUF models. The integration is completely non-functional.

signals.topic: MCP SSE server restart breaks Continue communication without automatic session re-establishment
signals.summary: When an MCP server using SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport is restarted, Continue attempts to reuse the old session instead of requesting a new one. This permanently breaks communication until Continue is manually restarted, disrupting workflows that involve MCP servers that restart periodically.
aliases: MCP session stale after server restart
signals.review_reason: P1 — MCP tools are a key Continue feature. When an MCP server restarts (a common operational scenario for containerized or remotely hosted MCPs), Continue becomes permanently non-functional until manually restarted. Count=1 but the session state bug is a clear user pain with a well-described mechanism. Not P2 because MCP functionality is central to Continue's value proposition and the workaround (manual restart) is disruptive.

source_issues.title: (sse) mcp restarts breaks communication
source_issues.evidence: User reports that after an MCP server restart, Continue does not re-establish a session and continues using the old (now invalid) session. Communication breaks entirely. HTTP streaming protocol may not have this issue — specific to SSE transport.

signals.topic: crewai 依赖 lancedb 导致 Intel Mac 上完全无法安装
signals.summary: crewai 1.12.2 将 lancedb>=0.29.2 设为强制依赖，但该版本的 lancedb 已停止发布 macOS x86_64 wheel，导致 Intel Mac 用户 pip install crewai 直接失败，Product 安装流程被完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: Product 安装流程完全阻断，用户无法在 Intel Mac 上使用 crewai。即使不使用 memory 功能的用户也被强制要求安装 lancedb，而 lancedb 在该平台上无任何可用 wheel，属于高优先级阻断性问题。

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: pip install crewai==1.12.2 在 Intel Mac 上报 ResolutionImpossible。lancedb 0.29.2-0.30.2 均无 macOS x86_64 wheel。crewai 对 lancedb 的依赖是强制的（core dependency），即便项目不使用 memory 特性也被阻断。

signals.topic: OPENAI_API_KEY 环境变量在 CrewAI 运行时无法正确传递，导致 crew.kickoff() 报 401 认证失败
signals.summary: 用户在环境变量中正确配置了有效的 OPENAI_API_KEY，通过 Python 脚本和 curl 验证均可正常工作，但在执行 crew.kickoff() 时 CrewAI 内部运行时无法读取或传递该环境变量，导致所有 OpenAI LLM 调用报 401 invalid_api_key，主流程完全阻断。
aliases: OPENAI_API_KEY env var not propagated inside crew execution
API key 401 authentication failure inside Crew
API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI
signals.review_reason: crew.kickoff() 是 CrewAI 的核心入口，用户配置了正确密钥后主流程依然无法运行，属于主流程阻断型 bug。即使是单一报告，API key 认证失败直接导致整个 Crew 无法执行，具有高优先级。

source_issues.title: [BUG] OpenAI API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI with 401 invalid_api_key
source_issues.evidence: 同一 OPENAI_API_KEY 在外部 Python 脚本和 curl 中验证正常，但在 crew.kickoff() 执行时报 401 invalid_api_key。CrewAI 在工具验证阶段通过（说明 key 格式可读），但 agent 调用 OpenAI API 时失败。推测 CrewAI 子进程/agent 执行环境中环境变量传递异常。

signals.topic: Task retry 时 tool 重新执行缺少幂等性保护，可能导致重复支付、重复发送邮件、重复交易
signals.summary: 当 Task 因异常失败而重试（max_retry_limit、exception handling 或外部重触发）时，已成功执行的 @tool 函数会再次运行，因为没有任何机制检测特定 tool 调用是否已完成。导致 Stripe 扣款、邮件发送、API 交易等副作用重复触发，造成直接经济损失。
aliases: tool re-execution no idempotency guard on retry
tool side effects fire twice on retry
signals.review_reason: 工具重复执行直接导致可量化的经济损失（重复支付、重复邮件、重复交易），是典型的 cost loss 场景。issue 附有代码示例和 LangGraph Cloud 的独立复现确认，模式清晰。即使单仓单报告，影响明确且严重。

source_issues.title: Tool re-execution on task retry has no idempotency guard — duplicate payments, emails, trades possible
source_issues.evidence: issue 提供了复现步骤和代码示例：在 tool 成功执行后模拟后续步骤失败，Task retry 导致同一 @tool 再次执行。附 LangGraph Cloud issue #7417 作为独立第三方确认的同类失败模式（生产环境）。CrewAI 自身没有任何 dedup 机制。

signals.topic: output_pydantic / response_model 在 vLLM 等非 OpenAI LLM 的 tool-calling 循环中泄露，导致 tools 被跳过
signals.summary: 自 v1.9.0 起，Task.output_pydantic 被映射为 response_model 并在每次 tool-calling 循环迭代中传给 LLM。对于 vLLM（及其他 OpenAI-compatible 推理服务），LLM 在收到 response_format 时会跳过 tool 调用直接返回结构化 JSON，导致所有 @tool 永远不执行，工具功能对非 OpenAI 用户完全不可用。
aliases: response_model causes tools to be skipped on vLLM
structured output regresses vLLM tool calling
signals.review_reason: 对使用 vLLM 或其他 OpenAI-compatible LLM 的用户，关键功能（@tool）完全不可用，是功能性阻断。v1.9.0 的 structured outputs 支持变更导致 regression，影响所有非 OpenAI provider 用户。

source_issues.title: [BUG] output_pydantic / response_model leaks into agent tool-calling loop, causing tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
source_issues.evidence: v1.9.0 将 output_pydantic 从后处理改为传入 agent executor 的每次循环迭代。vLLM 等 LLM 在同时收到 tools 和 response_format 时会跳过 tool 调用直接返回 JSON，导致 _run() 从不执行。LiteLLM 的 response_model 处理逻辑完全绕过 tool-calling 机制。

signals.topic: crewai opentelemetry-sdk 版本锁定与 openlit 依赖冲突，导致可观测性集成失败
signals.summary: crewai 1.14.4 将 opentelemetry-sdk 锁定在 1.35.0，而 openlit 1.42.0 需要 >=1.38.0，使用 poetry 安装时直接报依赖冲突 error，用户无法同时使用 crewai 和 openlit 进行可观测性监控。
signals.review_reason: 依赖冲突导致使用 crewai + openlit 进行生产可观测性监控的用户无法完成安装，是明确的 integration break。虽然 count=1 且非核心安装，但 openlit 是生产监控的主流选择，冲突阻断了关键集成路径。

source_issues.title: [BUG] dependency conflict with OpenLIT
source_issues.evidence: poetry lock 阶段直接报依赖冲突：crewai 锁 opentelemetry-sdk==1.35.0，openlit 要求 >=1.38.0。提供了明确的复现步骤和 pyproject.toml 示例配置。

signals.topic: Silent session data loss — CLI loses user work without any warning or notification
signals.summary: When disk is full, sessions are auto-deleted after 30 days, or metadata corruption occurs, the CLI does not warn the user, resulting in complete loss of recorded session work.
signals.review_reason: 4 issues describe sessions being silently lost or unsaved with no user-facing warning. Users lose recorded work without any notification. Systemic problem affecting core recording functionality with explicit user impact evidence ('losing work without warning', 'silently stops', 'no UI notification'). Affects a fundamental user expectation: that recorded session history is preserved and accessible.

source_issues.title: Disk-full disables recording silently
source_issues.evidence: When disk is full, recording silently stops. User continues working but session is not saved — only a debug warning, no UI notification. User loses all unsaved work.

source_issues.title: Silent session deletion — 30-day retention is enabled by default
source_issues.evidence: Sessions are silently deleted after 30 days with no user-facing notification. User loses access to historical sessions without any warning.

source_issues.title: Corrupted metadata line can hide the whole session
source_issues.evidence: Corrupted first line of session file causes the entire session — including valid message history — to become inaccessible for listing and resume. Entire session effectively lost.

source_issues.title: Metadata-only sessions can be deleted immediately, regardless of age
source_issues.evidence: Sessions that have only metadata but no message content are deleted immediately regardless of age. If user lost content mid-session, the session is gone with no chance to recover.

signals.topic: Session metadata corruption makes valid sessions inaccessible — users cannot resume or list their work
signals.summary: Missing or corrupted session metadata fields (projectHash, metadata line) cause valid sessions with real content to become invisible to listing and resume commands, making recorded work effectively inaccessible.
signals.review_reason: 2 issues show valid session files with real content becoming inaccessible due to metadata corruption. Users cannot resume their own work even though files exist on disk. This blocks the core session resume workflow and can result in permanent loss of recorded conversation history.

source_issues.title: Missing projectHash makes a real JSONL session unlistable
source_issues.evidence: Valid session file with real message content becomes completely unlistable due to a missing projectHash field. CLI cannot find or resume a session that exists on disk with valid conversation history.

source_issues.title: File recreation drops the metadata line
source_issues.evidence: When a file is deleted and recreated, the metadata line is dropped. Results in corrupted session file that cannot be properly parsed, making recorded work inaccessible.

signals.topic: Sessions exist on disk but cannot be found or resumed — CLI gives contradictory session existence information
signals.summary: The CLI gives contradictory information about session existence depending on which command is used. --session-id says a session exists and directs user to --resume, but --resume fails for the same ID. Exit screen prints invalid resume commands.
signals.review_reason: Users receive contradictory information about session state from the CLI itself. The CLI says a session exists and directs the user to --resume, but --resume then fails. Exit screen prints invalid resume commands. This completely breaks the core session resume workflow and undermines user trust in CLI output.

source_issues.title: --session-id and --resume disagree about whether a session exists
source_issues.evidence: --session-id reports session already exists and tells user to use --resume, but --resume fails for the same session ID. sessionExists() and resolveSession() use different filtering logic giving contradictory results.

source_issues.title: Exit screen always prints a resume command without validation
source_issues.evidence: Exit screen always prints a resume command pointing to a session that may not exist or may not be valid. User cannot trust the printed command.

signals.topic: Symlink path creates isolated session store — same folder yields different sessions
signals.summary: Accessing the same physical folder through a symlink path creates a separate session store, causing sessions to be invisible when accessed from the resolved path.
signals.review_reason: Users working with symlinked project directories cannot find sessions they created. This is a real workflow impact for users with symlinked project structures, causing sessions to appear lost. While count=1, the scenario is a common development pattern and causes session visibility failures.

source_issues.title: Symlink path creates a different session store
source_issues.evidence: Same physical folder accessed via symlink vs resolved path creates separate session stores. Sessions created via symlink are invisible when accessed from the resolved path, causing session loss and confusion.

signals.topic: File editing produces damaged/junk content instead of intended single-file changes
signals.summary: When user requests a simple single-file edit, the agent produces a multi-edit with simultaneous replace strings that create junk content and damage the file.
signals.review_reason: Single instance with strong user impact evidence: the agent corrupted a file instead of making a requested edit, then silently halted without notification. File corruption and silent failure are clear user-perceivable problems. Even though count=1, the severity of user-visible damage (corrupted source file) and explicit user dissatisfaction warrants inclusion.

source_issues.title: Gemini suddenly lost the ability to edit a single Python file
source_issues.evidence: User requested a simple single-file edit. Agent prepared a multi-edit with three simultaneous replace strings that created junk content. Agent halted without notifying the user and made unhelpful or damaging edits. User explicitly reported being 'very disappointed'.

signals.topic: uv dependency resolution fails on Windows due to mlx[cpu] having no Windows wheels
signals.summary: Using `uv pip install -e "smolagents[dev] @ ."` on Windows (Python 3.11/3.12) fails with 'No solution found when resolving dependencies' because mlx[cpu] has no win_amd64 wheels. This blocks developers from installing and setting up the project locally.
aliases: mlx[cpu] no Windows wheels blocking dev install
uv pip install smolagents[dev] fails on Windows
signals.review_reason: This is a real, reproducible bug with full error logs and clear steps to reproduce. The mlx[cpu] package has no Windows wheels, making smolagents[dev] impossible to install on Windows via uv. This blocks contributor onboarding and local development — a clear developer experience degradation with cost impact (unable to set up dev environment). Count=1 but review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: both Python 3.11 and 3.12 tested, explicit 'No solution found' error, user explicitly offered to submit a PR.

source_issues.title: BUG: No solution found when resolving dependencies while uv
source_issues.evidence: User tried to install smolagents[dev] with `uv pip install -e "smolagents[dev] @ ."` on Windows Python 3.11 and 3.12. Both fail with 'No solution found when resolving dependencies' because mlx[cpu] has no win_amd64 wheels. The dev dependency chain is unsatisfiable on Windows, preventing any local development setup.

signals.topic: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with ValueError when parsing output with colons
signals.summary: BaseSandbox.grep() in sandbox.py uses `line.split(":", 2)` to parse grep output as `path:line:text`. When file paths contain colons or when OCI runtime errors contain colons, `int(parts[1])` raises ValueError, crashing the tool node and terminating the agent run. The bug has 4 independent user reports across two distinct trigger conditions (colons in file paths; OCI runtime error messages), both from external users with reproducible examples.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（agent run被终止）+ 4条独立外部用户报告 + 有完整堆栈和可复现示例。两种触发条件（文件名含冒号、OCI运行时错误含冒号）均指向同一根因：grep输出解析逻辑在冒号场景下崩溃。这是SandboxBackend的核心文件搜索工具，crash直接导致agent任务中断。

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.grep() crashes with ValueError when file paths contain colons
source_issues.evidence: Crashes when searching files with colon-containing paths (e.g., timestamp filenames). Stack trace: ValueError at int(parts[1]). External user hmmailong147 with reproducible example.

source_issues.title: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with ValueError when container exec fails
source_issues.evidence: OCI runtime exec failure (e.g., missing workdir) returns error text with colons, parsed as grep output. ValueError at int(parts[1]). External user pierrel with Docker repro.

source_issues.title: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with ValueError when container exec fails (parses OCI runtime error as grep output)
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #3441. Closed as duplicate by reporter; original refiled as #3441.

source_issues.title: SandboxBackend.grep crashes with ValueError when container exec fails (parses OCI runtime error as grep output)
source_issues.evidence: First filing of the OCI runtime error crash. Closed by reporter in favor of #3440 which followed the bug report template.

signals.topic: DeepAgents agent.invoke 比 LangChain 慢 34 倍（349s vs 10s），单次 LLM 调用耗时 566s
signals.summary: 外部用户报告在相同模型、相同工具配置下，deepagents agent.invoke 的响应时间（349s）远超原生 LangChain llm.bind_tools 调用（10s），差距达 34 倍。单次 LLM 调用实际耗时 566s，远超正常范围。这导致主流程严重延迟，造成明显的时间成本损失。
signals.review_reason: 显著成本损失（349s 延迟 vs 10s 基线），单仓 count=1 但证据非常具体：用户提供完整 benchmark 数据，OpenAI/LangChain/DeepAgents 三方对比，差距达 34 倍。符合主流程性能劣化、关键功能不可用（agent 响应极慢）的痛点定义。count=1 按规则默认不 P0，但 review_reason 给出强用户影响证据（巨大延迟差距），维持 P1。

source_issues.title: Slow response with agent.invoke
source_issues.evidence: 外部用户 pku-wuwei 提供完整对比数据：OpenAI direct=6.3s, LangChain=10.1s, DeepAgents=349.3s。deepagents 比 LangChain 慢 34 倍，单次 LLM 调用 566s。工具仅增加数秒延迟，主要耗时在 agent.invoke 内部。deepagents 0.6.1, Python 3.12.3。

signals.topic: CompositeBackend.als() 返回错误目录路径，导致 SkillsMiddleware 技能加载失败
signals.summary: 当调用 CompositeBackend.als() 时，如果传入路径恰好等于一个已注册的路由（如 /memory/skills/），返回值中的路径会被错误地拼接成 /memory/skills/memory/ 而非正确的 /memory/skills/test_skill/。根因是 _route_for_path 在精确匹配时返回 backend_path = "/"，而 StoreBackend 返回的是绝对路径，_remap_file_info_path 错误地为其添加了完整路由前缀，导致路径重复。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用（SkillsMiddleware 无法正确加载技能）+ 有根因分析和可复现代码 + 外部用户报告。虽然 count=1，但 review_reason 给出明确用户影响证据（技能加载失败），符合 P1 标准。

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend.als() returns wrong directory when path exactly matches a registered route
source_issues.evidence: 外部用户 snakeytm 提供可复现示例。根因分析详细：_route_for_path 在精确匹配时返回 backend_path="/"，_remap_file_info_path 错误拼接路径段。受影响场景：SkillsMiddleware 通过 CompositeBackend 路由加载技能时失败或返回错误路径。

signals.topic: JavaScript 解释器工具不等待 async IIFE 返回值，返回未解析的 Promise handle
signals.summary: deepagents 内置的 JavaScript 解释器（quickjs）支持顶层 await，但当 async IIFE 作为最终表达式时，不对其返回值进行 await，导致语义等价的两段代码行为不一致：(async () => { return await x; })() 返回 [object]（未解析 Promise），而先赋值再引用则正常返回结果。许多模型默认使用 IIFE 模式，导致用户在正常使用中频繁遇到此问题。
aliases: interpreter returns Promise instead of value
signals.review_reason: 体验下降（解释器结果不一致，IIFE 模式返回值类型错误），非主流程阻断但影响常见 JS 代码执行模式。外部用户 evan-rash 提供了清晰的对比用例和根因分析。由于 count=1、非高频，按规则默认为 P2，维持 P2。

source_issues.title: Bug: eval interpreter tool does not await async IIFE return values
source_issues.evidence: 外部用户 evan-rash 提供两个可对比的最小复现用例（顶层 await 正常 vs async IIFE 返回 handle）+ 根因分析。许多模型倾向于默认使用 IIFE 模式，用户正常使用中频繁遇到此行为不一致问题。

signals.topic: ChatOpenRouter creates fresh httpx clients per instantiation causing socket leaks in production deployments
signals.summary: ChatOpenRouter constructs a new httpx.Client/AsyncClient pair for every model instance with no caching or connection pooling. In common production patterns (LangGraph factory graphs, FastAPI per-request instantiation), this leaks TLS sockets linearly with each request and exhausts OS-level socket limits. The same bug was previously fixed for AzureChatOpenAI in PR #32531.
signals.review_reason: Production-blocking resource leak: every ChatOpenRouter instantiation leaks TLS connections that are never returned to the pool. In LangGraph factory graph pattern (documented, per-request instantiation) and FastAPI dependency injection, this causes socket exhaustion well before model rate limits. Confirmed by two independent reports from the same author with reproducible test using psutil socket counting. The same bug class was previously fixed for AzureChatOpenAI (PR #32531), confirming the pattern is well-understood.

source_issues.title: langchain-openrouter: ChatOpenRouter creates fresh httpx clients per instantiation (no default-client caching)
source_issues.evidence: Reporter provided reproducible script using psutil to count ESTABLISHED TCP connections. After 20 fresh ChatOpenRouter instances, socket count grows linearly and does not return to baseline after del+gc.collect(). Production impact: LangGraph factory graphs (documented per-request pattern) and FastAPI DI create fresh models per request, exhausting OS socket limits in production.

source_issues.title: langchain-openrouter: ChatOpenRouter creates fresh httpx clients per instantiation (no default-client caching)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #37498 by same author. Confirms same socket leak issue with additional detail on the openai/openai-python#763 streaming connection pool bug compounding the problem.

signals.topic: LLM response `.choices[0]` accessed without empty-list guard causes IndexError on content-filtered responses
