signals.summary: Multiple files in the langchain codebase directly access `response.choices[0]` or `response.choices[0].message` without checking whether the `choices` list is empty. When LLM providers return an empty `choices` list due to content filtering, quota limits, or streaming edge cases, this produces an `IndexError` instead of a meaningful error message. The bug is confirmed for Azure OpenAI and Gemini 2.5 Flash on safety events, and is a known pattern across the codebase.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: LLM calls with content filtering silently crash with IndexError instead of a meaningful message. While only 1 issue, the bug pattern is described as widespread across multiple files in the codebase. No error message is shown to the user — just an unhandled IndexError — making this a high-impact user experience failure.

source_issues.title: bug: LLM response .choices[0] accessed without empty-list guard
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed IndexError when LLM returns empty choices on content filtering (OpenAI content_filter, Azure OpenAI, Gemini 2.5 Flash safety events). Reporter provided exact code pattern showing unguarded access in multiple files, with PR #37516 ready as fix.

signals.topic:
Ollama multimodal message text content incorrectly prefixed with `
` causing silent empty responses from vision models
signals.summary:
In langchain-ollama, `_convert_messages_to_ollama_messages` unconditionally prepends `
` to every text segment in list-format content. For multimodal messages (text + image), this causes vision models sensitive to exact prompt formatting to silently return empty responses with no error or warning. Confirmed with deepseek-ocr which requires single-line prompts.
signals.review_reason: Key multimodal feature broken: Ollama vision/OCR use cases silently fail with empty responses and no error message. Users running deepseek-ocr (or any prompt-formatting-sensitive vision model) on local Ollama get zero output with no indication of what went wrong. This is a critical function failure for image understanding workflows.

source_issues.title: fix(ollama): multimodal message text content incorrectly prefixed with \n
source_issues.evidence: Reporter provided minimal reproducible example with 1x1 base64 PNG showing the newline prefix bug. Confirmed impact: deepseek-ocr silently returns empty response when content starts with \n. The failure is completely invisible — no error, no warning, just empty output — making it extremely hard to debug. OCR and image understanding use cases are completely broken for Ollama.

signals.topic: Chroma.update_document() rejects Document objects with omitted metadata, while add_documents() accepts the same input
signals.summary: Chroma's update_document() raises ValueError when passed a Document without explicit metadata, while add_documents() handles the same Document structure successfully. This API inconsistency blocks a common workflow where users want to update document content without touching metadata.
signals.review_reason: Common workflow blocked: updating a document's content without modifying metadata is a natural use case that works in add_documents() but fails in update_document() with a confusing ValueError. The inconsistency between add and update paths means users cannot use the same Document objects across both operations, requiring awkward workarounds like explicitly passing metadata={}.

source_issues.title: `Chroma.update_document()` fails when `Document` metadata is omitted
source_issues.evidence: Reporter provided full reproduction script: add_documents() accepts Document(page_content='...') without metadata, but update_document() raises ValueError: Expected metadata to be a non-empty dict, got 0 metadata attributes. The bug is in the update path in langchain_chroma/vectorstores.py where metadata is forwarded without normalizing None to empty dict. 11 comments indicate active community interest.

signals.topic: Thread copy API endpoint blocks synchronously for 12+ minutes, no async/progress/shallow-copy option
signals.summary: The `/threads/{thread_id}/copy` endpoint is entirely synchronous and blocks for large conversations. Observed copies take over 12 minutes. No async mode, no progress indicator, no shallow-copy option. This directly breaks production deployments on serverless platforms like AWS Lambda (15-minute hard timeout), leaving the app in an uncertain state when the timeout is hit.
aliases: long-running thread copy no async option
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is directly blocked. Observed 12+ minute sync operation with hard production timeout (Lambda 15-min limit) causing uncertain state. Not theoretical — user has concrete failure data. This is a P0: production-critical feature is unusable on common serverless infrastructure.

source_issues.title: Thread copy endpoint can take 12+ minutes with no async/progress or shallow-copy option
source_issues.evidence: User reports copy taking over 12 minutes. Endpoint is synchronous with no async mode. AWS Lambda 15-minute timeout directly hit, leaving app in uncertain state. No way to estimate cost before starting, no progress, no shallow copy option.

signals.topic: HttpClient.request_reconnect reuses Content-Length/Content-Type headers on body-less GET retry, causing h11.LocalProtocolError
signals.summary: The langgraph_sdk HttpClient's request_reconnect method incorrectly reuses Content-Length and Content-Type headers when retrying a GET request that had no body. The HTTP/1.1 protocol does not allow these headers on body-less GET, causing an h11.LocalProtocolError. Affects runs.wait and runs.cancel(wait=True) code paths.
aliases: HTTP client retry header reuse bug
h11 protocol error on SDK reconnect
signals.review_reason: Confirmed SDK bug with reproducible minimal example. Causes h11.LocalProtocolError at runtime during retry operations — breaks runs.wait and runs.cancel(wait=True) workflows. Not a P0 only because count=1 and single-repository scope, but impact is clear: connection failures in core SDK retry paths.

source_issues.title: langgraph_sdk: HttpClient.request_reconnect reuses Content-Length/Content-Type on body-less GET retry, causing h11.LocalProtocolError
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible bug in langgraph_sdk 0.3.14 and main. HttpClient.request_reconnect sends headers (Content-Length, Content-Type) on a body-less GET retry, violating HTTP/1.1 spec and causing h11.LocalProtocolError. Affected: runs.wait and runs.cancel(wait=True). User provided minimal reproducible example.

signals.topic: AsyncSqliteSaver.put() and put_writes() deadlock instead of raising when called synchronously from within the event loop
signals.summary: AsyncSqliteSaver methods put() and put_writes() deadlock (hang indefinitely) when called synchronously from within the async event loop, instead of raising asyncio.InvalidStateError. Only delete_thread() correctly raises the exception. This makes the API inconsistent and causes hard-to-debug hangs in workflows that accidentally call these methods from sync context.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed deadlock bug with reproducible code. When called from sync context inside event loop, put() and put_writes() silently deadlock rather than raising an error. This is a critical reliability issue: workflows hang with no error signal, requiring process restart to recover.

source_issues.title: AsyncSqliteSaver.put() and put_writes() deadlock instead of raising when called synchronously from within the event loop
source_issues.evidence: User-provided self-contained reproducible example. put() and put_writes() hang indefinitely (deadlock) when called from sync context inside event loop. delete_thread() correctly raises asyncio.InvalidStateError, showing the expected behavior. API is inconsistent: some methods detect the invalid call, others deadlock silently.

signals.topic: RetryPolicy jitter added after max_interval cap, violating documented contract — sleep_time can exceed max_interval by up to 1 second per retry
signals.summary: RetryPolicy computes backoff correctly but adds jitter AFTER applying the max_interval cap, so sleep_time can silently exceed max_interval by up to 1 second per retry. This violates the documented contract of max_interval. Users relying on max_interval for cost/rate control get unpredictable retry timing.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed logic bug in retry policy: jitter is applied after the max_interval cap, silently violating the documented contract. Users who set max_interval for rate limiting or cost control will experience retry delays that exceed their configuration. Impact is systemic — both sync and async retry paths affected.

source_issues.title: bug: RetryPolicy jitter can cause sleep to exceed max_interval
source_issues.evidence: Code shows: interval = min(max_interval, ...) then sleep_time = interval + random.uniform(0,1). Jitter added AFTER cap, so max_interval is violated by up to 1 second per retry. User provided reproduction showing sleep_time reaching ~2.0s when max_interval=1.0s. Both sync and async retry paths affected.

signals.topic: YAML docstring parser crashes on colons without quotes, spamming warning logs on every API route at startup
signals.summary: langgraph-api's docstring-to-OpenAPI parser uses yaml.safe_load on endpoint docstrings. When a docstring contains colons not in quoted strings (e.g., 'Query params:'), YAML interprets it as a mapping key and throws ScannerError. The result is a warning printed for every API route on every startup, obscuring real log entries and degrading the developer experience.
signals.review_reason: Operational bug: every API route at startup generates a full stack trace warning in logs. This is not just cosmetic — it pollutes logs, obscures real errors, and degrades the developer experience significantly. Affects all LangGraph API deployments.

source_issues.title: LangGraph console docstring warnings: yaml.scanner.ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here
source_issues.evidence: On every langgraph-api launch (v0.8.7+), logs are spammed with ScannerError for every route whose docstring contains unquoted colons (e.g. 'Query params:'). Full stack trace printed per route. User shows example: 'Unable to parse docstring from OpenAPI schema for route /assistants/{assistant_id} (delete_assistant): mapping values are not allowed here'. Reproducible on any LangGraph app launch.

signals.topic: Knowledge base UI components render with unexpected errors in multiple contexts
signals.summary: Knowledge base pages and related UI components fail to render correctly, showing 'An unexpected error occurred while rendering this component' across different contexts including pop-up pages and knowledge retrieval test panels. Affects both self-hosted Docker and cloud deployments.
aliases: knowledge retrieval test component render error
UI component unexpected error knowledge base
signals.review_reason: Two issues with the same rendering error pattern in knowledge base components. While not blocking all usage, the knowledge retrieval test is a core workflow for building RAG applications, and the error affects both cloud and self-hosted deployments, indicating a systematic rendering issue.

source_issues.title: Pop-up page rendering error
source_issues.evidence: User encounters 'An unexpected error occurred while rendering this component' when viewing pop-up pages in Dify 1.14.1 self-hosted Docker deployment. Screenshots show the broken UI state.

source_issues.title: Knowledge Retrieval Test, An unexpected error occurred while rendering this component.
source_issues.evidence: Knowledge Retrieval Test component fails to render with 'An unexpected error occurred while rendering this component' in Dify 1.14.1 cloud and self-hosted Docker deployments. User cannot test knowledge retrieval, a core Dify feature.

signals.topic: PostgreSQL silent data loss on Docker Desktop WSL2 after extended uptime
signals.summary: Docker Desktop WSL2 deployments suffer silent data loss where PostgreSQL returns empty query results after 2-3 days of continuous uptime, even though data files exist on disk. Container restart restores all data. Caused by 9p stale file handles in bind mounts.
signals.review_reason: This is a silent data loss bug that directly causes data to become inaccessible for days before users notice empty dashboards. The 'silent' nature (no error shown, data on disk intact) makes it especially dangerous for production self-hosted deployments. Docker Desktop WSL2 is a popular development environment, amplifying the impact.

source_issues.title: PostgreSQL bind mount causes silent data loss on Docker Desktop WSL2 due to 9p stale file handles
source_issues.evidence: After ~2-3 days of uptime, PostgreSQL returns empty query results for all tables (0 apps, 0 datasets, 0 workflows, 0 tenants, 0 accounts). Data exists on disk but is unreadable. Container restart restores data immediately. Affects default docker-compose.yaml with bind mount on Docker Desktop WSL2.

signals.topic: TTS auto-play only reads the last sentence on Windows/Docker deployments
signals.summary: When TTS feature is enabled with auto-play in agent Debug & Preview, only the last sentence of the response is spoken instead of the full message. Multiple related issues spanning versions indicate this is a widespread persistent problem.
signals.review_reason: This is a recurring bug affecting the TTS core feature across multiple versions and deployment environments (Windows, Docker). The issue explicitly references 6 prior related issues, confirming high frequency and broad user impact. The core TTS playback feature is broken for a key use case (auto-play in chat).

source_issues.title: Collection of TTS, Auto-play, Windows, Docker, Delayed Start Issues
source_issues.evidence: User loads a model with TTS feature enabled in agent Debug & Preview, turns on auto-play, and prompts the agent to tell a joke. Only the last sentence is heard. Issue references 6 prior related issues (#13759, #33918, #34542, #10076, #17919, #27848), indicating a long-standing, widespread problem across multiple users and versions with no clear solution.

signals.topic: Variable type silently converts Number to Integer in multi-turn ChatFlow conversations
signals.summary: Number variables set to float values (e.g., 0.0) are silently converted to integers during multi-turn conversations, causing 'not supported value type integer' errors and blocking workflow execution from the second turn onward.
aliases: float to int silent conversion ChatFlow
signals.review_reason: This bug silently corrupts variable types in multi-turn conversations, causing workflows to fail from the second turn onward with a cryptic 'not supported value type integer' error. The silent nature (first turn succeeds, second fails) makes debugging difficult for affected users. It blocks a core ChatFlow feature entirely.

source_issues.title: Error: not supported value type integer because cannot init a float var
source_issues.evidence: User initializes a conversation variable as Number (0.0) in ChatFlow. First turn works fine. On second turn, the Number variable silently changes to Integer type, causing 'not supported value type integer' error at variable_factory.py#L68. Workflow execution is blocked from second turn onward. Root cause identified in variable_factory.py variable type inference logic.

signals.topic: Perplexity Sonar credentials cannot be deleted and model validation fails incorrectly
signals.summary: Using the OpenAI-API-compatible provider with Perplexity Sonar models leaves broken credential references. Users cannot delete credentials (system claims they are in use but shows 'Credential with id xxx not found'), reinstalling the provider re-adds deleted models, and new Sonar model validation incorrectly fails with 'max_tokens must be at least 16 for sonar'.
aliases: deleted Sonar models reappear after reinstall
signals.review_reason: Credential management operations are entirely broken for Perplexity Sonar users: cannot delete credentials, deleted models reappear on reinstall, and validation fails incorrectly. This blocks users from properly configuring and maintaining their LLM provider integrations in the cloud deployment scenario.

source_issues.title: OpenAI-API-compatible provider keeps broken Perplexity Sonar credentials and validation fails
source_issues.evidence: User adds Perplexity Sonar models via OpenAI-API-compatible provider, then deletes credentials. System reports credentials are in use but opening credential config shows 'Credential with id xxx not found'. Reinstalling provider automatically re-adds deleted Sonar models. Adding a new Sonar model with a new credential fails validation incorrectly with 'max_tokens must be at least 16 for sonar'. Core credential management operations are completely broken.

signals.topic: xai LLM provider crashes with AttributeError on every factory construction — tools silently dropped
signals.summary: The xai LLM provider (Grok) has three bugs: (1) constructor unconditionally reads `self.config.xai_base_url` on `BaseLlmConfig` which lacks that attribute, causing AttributeError on every `LlmFactory.create('xai')` call; (2) `generate_response()` drops `tools` and `tool_choice` without forwarding them to the API; (3) missing `_parse_response` helper causes tool-call payload to be dropped. The provider is completely non-functional through the factory path.
signals.review_reason: P0: xai provider is completely broken through the factory — every user hitting LlmFactory.create('xai') gets AttributeError and cannot use the provider at all. Tools are silently dropped even after the crash is worked around. Single issue but with extremely clear, reproducible, blocking evidence.

source_issues.title: xai LLM provider: tools silently dropped, AttributeError on factory construction
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError on every LlmFactory.create('xai') call; tools never forwarded to API; tool-call payload unrecoverable. Reproducer provided. Affects main code path for xai (Grok) users.

signals.topic: mem0-ts OpenAIEmbedder silently produces wrong-dimension vectors with OpenAI-compatible proxies (LiteLLM/vLLM/Ollama) — causes vector store rejection
signals.summary: mem0-ts OpenAIEmbedder does not pass `encoding_format: 'float'` to the OpenAI embeddings API. The Node openai SDK v4.x defaults to base64 encoding. Against OpenAI-compatible proxies (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama, OpenRouter), the proxy returns JSON floats but the SDK attempts to base64-decode them, producing invalid 192-dim vectors instead of the expected dimension. The vector store then rejects with 'Vector dimension error' and recall search fails silently with 'Bad Request'.
aliases: mem0-ts OpenAI-compatible proxy vector dimension error
signals.review_reason: P0: TS SDK embedder silently produces wrong-dimension vectors with very common proxy setups (LiteLLM/vLLM/Ollama). User sees 'Bad Request' on recall search with no hint at root cause. Confirmed reproduction with exact vector lengths. Affects a core integration path (OpenAI-compatible embeddings).

source_issues.title: Bug: OpenAIEmbedder in mem0-ts fails with OpenAI-compatible proxies (encoding_format default base64) — port #4058 to TS SDK
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows len:192 vs expected len:768 with LiteLLM+vLLM; recall search fails with 'Bad Request'; known affected backends: LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama, OpenRouter; Python side already fixed via #4058 but TS port never done.

signals.topic: Memory.update() silently drops all custom metadata on every non-MongoDB vector store — data loss regression
signals.summary: Memory.update() and AsyncMemory.update() silently discard all custom metadata fields (category, priority, source, bucket_id, etc.) on Qdrant, Pinecone, Milvus, PGVector, Supabase, Redis, FAISS, Chroma, and Weaviate. Only a 5-field whitelist (user_id, agent_id, run_id, actor_id, role) is preserved. No error or warning is raised. The bug was previously fixed for MongoDB in #4495, the cross-provider follow-up was acknowledged but never completed, and it was re-introduced in the V3 pipeline rewrite via #4805.
aliases: custom metadata lost on update non-MongoDB
signals.review_reason: P0: Silent data loss affecting Memory.update() across 10+ vector store backends. User-provided custom metadata is silently discarded with no error/warning. Full repro steps provided. Regression path documented. Core API data-loss on a write operation.

source_issues.title: _update_memory() still drops custom metadata on all non-MongoDB vector stores (follow-up from #4495 never completed, regressed in V3 pipeline)
source_issues.evidence: Full repro steps provided: add with metadata -> update -> metadata becomes None. Affects ALL non-MongoDB vector stores. Regression: #4495 fixed MongoDB, cross-provider fix acknowledged but never shipped, V3 rewrite (#4805) re-introduced the bug. No warning or error raised — silent data loss.

signals.topic: memory.add() crashes with 400 Bad Request when conversation exceeds embedding model token limit (8192 tokens)
signals.summary: memory.add() embeds the full raw conversation as a single string for Phase 1 existing-memory retrieval. If the conversation exceeds the embedding model's token limit (8192 for all OpenAI embedding models), the call fails with `openai.BadRequestError: maximum input length is 8192 tokens`. Phase 2 (LLM extraction) and Phase 3 (storage) are never reached. Additionally, even when the call does not crash, embedding a multi-topic conversation into a single vector produces poor recall — semantically distant but relevant existing memories are missed.
aliases: conversation too long blocks memory storage
signals.review_reason: P0: Complete pipeline failure on the core memory.add() operation when conversations exceed a common threshold. Hard crash with 400 Bad Request prevents any memory from being stored. Both Python and TypeScript SDK affected. Clear error trace provided.

source_issues.title: Raw conversation text embedded for existing-memory retrieval causes token limit crash and poor recall on multi-topic conversations
source_issues.evidence: Full error reproduced: openai.BadRequestError 400 'maximum input length is 8192 tokens'. Blocks the core memory.add() pipeline entirely when conversations are long. Also causes degraded recall even without crashing.

signals.topic: Memory.search() threshold filtering is inverted for distance-based vector stores — returns wrong results silently
signals.summary: The `threshold` parameter in Memory.search() assumes all stores return similarity scores (higher=better), but many stores return raw distance values (lower=better). Stores affected: pgvector (cosine distance), chroma (L2), redis (cosine distance), valkey, supabase, s3_vectors, vertex_ai, faiss (euclidean), azure_mysql, cassandra, milvus (L2). The threshold logic (`score >= threshold`) is inverted for distance stores — good matches (low distance) are filtered out, poor matches (high distance) are kept. Weaviate, Qdrant, Pinecone, and Elasticsearch are unaffected.
aliases: search threshold broken for chroma redis pgvector
threshold filtering wrong for distance-based stores
signals.review_reason: P1: Threshold filtering silently returns wrong/inverted results across 11+ vector store backends. Core search functionality produces incorrect results without any error. Well-documented with root cause, affected stores table, and code references. Downgraded from P0 because count=1 and results are returned (just wrong), not a hard block.

source_issues.title: fix: threshold filtering broken for distance-based vector stores
source_issues.evidence: Threshold logic is inverted for 11+ distance-based stores. Good matches dropped, bad matches kept. PGVector example: distance=0.05 -> score=0.05 >= 0.7 is False -> filtered out; distance=0.85 -> score=0.85 >= 0.7 is True -> kept. Stores already confirmed affected: pgvector, chroma, redis, valkey, supabase, s3_vectors, vertex_ai, faiss, azure_mysql, cassandra, milvus. Multiple prior partial PRs exist (#3840, #3804, #3994).

signals.topic: AG-UI multi-turn tool calls fail with 400 error on Foundry endpoints for both Responses API and Chat Completions API
signals.summary: Multi-turn tool-calling conversations break on the second turn onward when using agent-framework-ag-ui with Foundry project endpoints. The first tool-call turn works, but subsequent turns produce 400 BadRequestError because conversation history replay drops or mispairs tool result messages before sending back to the LLM. This affects all four AG-UI features (Agentic Chat, Human-in-the-Loop, Shared State, Agentic Generative UI) and makes AG-UI effectively unusable for any multi-turn tool-calling scenario in Python.
aliases: Foundry endpoint tool result message dropped in history replay
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：所有 AG-UI 多轮对话在首次工具调用后完全失败，返回 400 错误。影响所有 4 种 AG-UI 功能特性，用户需手动 workaround（子类化 AgentFrameworkAgent 注入缺失工具结果），且文档未提及此限制。这不是边缘场景，而是核心集成路径的完全阻断。

source_issues.title: Python: Multi-turn tool calls fail with both Responses API and Chat Completions API when used via agent-framework-ag-ui (Foundry project endpoint)
source_issues.evidence: First turn tool call works; second turn fails with 'No tool output found for function call' (Responses API) or 'must be followed by tool messages' (Chat Completions API). Affects all 4 AG-UI features. Cited 6 related open issues (#3304, #2699, #3010, #4213, #3331) indicating recurring pattern.

signals.topic: Azure Functions hosting requires user-defined dummy OrchestrationTrigger to expose agent endpoint
signals.summary: When using Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.AzureFunctions, the agent HTTP endpoint is never exposed unless the user adds at least one dummy [OrchestrationTrigger] function to their own assembly. Every consumer of this package hits this papercut because the Durable Task extension discovery only scans the user's assembly.
aliases: Azure Functions hosting startup failure missing OrchestrationTrigger
signals.review_reason: 每个 Azure Functions 用户都遇到此问题，代理端点完全不可用。错误信息不指向根本原因（需用户自己添加 dummy orchestrator），导致部署体验极差。虽然 count=1，但这是该包使用路径上的必经阻断点，实际影响覆盖所有 .NET Azure Functions 用户。

source_issues.title: .NET: Hosting.AzureFunctions requires a user-defined dummy [OrchestrationTrigger] to start
source_issues.evidence: Logs show 'Generating 0 job function(s)' and 'No HTTP routes mapped' — endpoint never exposed. Full startup logs and minimal repro provided. Every user of the package must add a dummy no-op orchestrator as a workaround.

signals.topic: Auto function calling strips null arguments from tool calls, causing required parameter failures
signals.summary: When using auto function calling, null arguments that the model generates are silently removed before function invocation. If the parameter is required (no default, non-nullable), the function fails to be invoked with an argument parsing error, breaking agent tool use workflows.
aliases: Auto function calling null argument removal breaks required parameters
signals.review_reason: 自动工具调用是核心功能，null 参数被静默删除导致必需参数函数调用失败。虽然是单例问题，但影响所有使用 auto function calling 且模型产生 null 值作为合法输入的场景，属于核心功能的明确 bug，reproduced 标签证明可复现。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Auto function calling removes null arguments
source_issues.evidence: Model generates {"location":"Seattle","unit":null} but inspection shows function call output is 'Argument parsing failed'. Has 'reproduced' label confirming the bug is verified. Agent tool use fails silently for valid null parameter values.

signals.topic: FileSystemJsonCheckPointStore.RetrieveIndexAsync returns all entries instead of filtering by sessionId
signals.summary: RetrieveIndexAsync(sessionId) returns all checkpoint entries from index.jsonl instead of filtering to only entries belonging to the specified session. This breaks session isolation in durable workflow checkpoint storage.
aliases: Checkpoint store session filtering broken RetrieveIndexAsync
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：checkpoint 存储的 session 隔离被完全破坏，所有会话都能看到彼此的 checkpoint 状态。严重影响多用户场景和 session 级别的状态隔离，具有 reproduced 标签确认可复现。

source_issues.title: .NET: FileSystemJsonCheckPointStore RetrieveIndexAsync() returns all checkpoint entries instead of filtering by SessionId
source_issues.evidence: Method signature takes sessionId parameter but implementation ignores it. Has 'reproduced' label. Breaks session isolation — a critical property for multi-user/durable workflow scenarios.

signals.topic: A2A task_id/message_id mapping was reverted causing incorrect field assignment in AgentResponseUpdate
signals.summary: A previous fix for A2A task_id/message_id mapping (fix #5288) was accidentally reverted in later code. The current implementation assigns task_id to AgentResponseUpdate.response_id but fails to assign message_id to AgentResponseUpdate.message_id, breaking A2A protocol correctness.
aliases: A2A message_id not assigned to AgentResponseUpdate.message_id
signals.review_reason: A2A 协议正确性 bug：message_id 未被正确赋值给 AgentResponseUpdate.message_id，破坏了 A2A 协议字段映射的语义。由于是 regression（之前 #5288 修复过），说明此行为不稳定。且 A2A 是框架的标准化互操作协议，关键字段映射错误会影响跨系统集成。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: [A2A] Correctly Handle task_id and message_id Returned by A2A
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly references previous fix #5288 that was reverted. User questions whether this is intentional or accidental. Has 'reproduced' label confirming the regression exists.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 在非沙箱环境下执行 LLM 生成的代码，存在任意代码执行风险
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 将 LLM 生成的代码直接写入磁盘并通过 subprocess 执行，无任何沙箱、文件系统隔离或网络限制。虽然初始化时发出 UserWarning，但该警告在生产配置中（如 -W ignore 或日志管道过滤）可被静默吞掉，导致用户可能在不知情的情况下部署到生产环境，面临完整系统被入侵、凭据被盗或数据销毁的风险。
signals.review_reason: 该漏洞直接导致生产环境中用户代码执行防护失效，攻击路径清晰（LLM被间接提示注入后生成恶意代码 → 无沙箱直接执行 → 完整系统入侵），后果严重（凭据盗窃、横向移动、数据销毁），影响 AutoGen 核心代码执行功能，为用户高频使用的组件，属于主流程阻断性安全风险。

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes via subprocess_exec without sandboxing. UserWarning is emitted at init but is trivially silenced in production (e.g. -W ignore). Full system compromise, credential theft, lateral movement, and data destruction are all possible attack outcomes per the issue.

signals.topic: MultimodalWebSurfer 未对网页标题进行净化处理，存在间接提示注入攻击风险
signals.summary: MultimodalWebSurfer agent 将网页 <title> 标签和 URL 等攻击者可控的元数据直接嵌入 LLM 提示词，缺少任何净化或边界标记。攻击者可构造恶意网页，通过标题内容进行社会工程学式提示注入，引导 Agent 访问钓鱼 URL（窃取会话 token）或执行未授权操作。
aliases: Web Surfer indirect prompt injection via page title
unsanitized webpage metadata in agent prompts
signals.review_reason: 该漏洞影响 AutoGen 核心 Web 导航功能（WebSurfer），攻击面广（任意网站均可发起间接提示注入），攻击手法隐蔽（通过页面标题而非显式指令进行注入），利用后可直接导致用户会话 token 泄露或 Agent 被劫持，属于关键信任边界破坏，且为 OWASP ASI-01 级别的已知安全风险分类。

source_issues.title: [Security] Web Surfer agent vulnerable to indirect prompt injection via page title
source_issues.evidence: MultimodalWebSurfer embeds page.title() output (attacker-controlled <title> tag) directly into LLM prompts without sanitization. Attackers can inject social-engineering payloads via crafted page titles to redirect agents to phishing URLs. CWE-94 and OWASP ASI-01 cited. Severity rated MEDIUM/HIGH.

signals.topic: AutoGen 缺少标准化工具调用拦截机制，无法在执行前对工具调用进行策略审计和参数过滤
signals.summary: AutoGen 在 Agent 决定调用工具与工具实际执行之间缺少标准化的拦截钩子。社区已在多个 issue（#6017、#5891、#5921）中明确指出这一gap，导致企业用户无法在生产环境中对工具调用进行策略审批、审计日志记录、参数改写和合规过滤，限制了 AutoGen 在企业场景的落地。
aliases: lack of tool call approval/audit hooks
signals.review_reason: 虽然该问题尚处于 RFC 阶段，未有用户报告实际生产事故，但其用户影响已被多个社区 issue 交叉确认：企业用户缺少工具调用审批和审计能力直接限制了 AutoGen 在合规要求严格的场景中部署，属于体验显著下降和关键功能不完整的痛点，置信度适当下调至 0.85。

source_issues.title: Proposal: GuardrailProvider protocol for tool call interception
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly cites 4 prior community issues (#6017, #5891, #5921, #5741) all identifying the same gap: no standardized hook between agent tool decision and tool execution. This blocks enterprise use cases requiring audit logging, rate limiting, and policy enforcement on tool calls.

signals.topic: VSCode extension aborts test run after a single slow (>10s) API test — all remaining tests never execute
signals.summary: The Playwright VSCode extension silently aborts the entire test run when encountering a slow API test (no browser activity events), dropping results from the UI and leaving subsequent tests in perpetual '○' (not run) state. Workaround is CLI, but IDE workflow is broken.
aliases: VSCode test explorer aborts on slow tests
API tests cause VSCode extension to silently drop remaining tests
signals.review_reason: VSCode extension IDE workflow is completely broken for any test suite containing slow API tests. All remaining tests silently never execute — not a degraded experience but a complete failure of the main flow. Clear reproduction with 80 tests and 23 dropped. CLI works as workaround, confirming it's an extension IPC issue, not a test logic issue.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: VSCode extension aborts run after a single slow (>10s) API test — subsequent tests never execute despite
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 80-test suite: first ~57 fast tests pass, then UI drops to 57/57 when first slow test (~17s) starts. All remaining tests (59-80) never run. CLI workaround works. Hypothesis: IPC heartbeat timeout shorter than per-test timeout.

signals.topic: Regression: install-deps --dry-run outputs human-readable text instead of executable commands, breaking CI/CD pipelines
signals.summary: v1.60.0 changed the output format of 'playwright install-deps --dry-run' from machine-executable shell commands to human-readable text, breaking automated CI/CD workflows that depended on parsing the output.
aliases: dry-run output no longer parseable by CI scripts
signals.review_reason: Clear regression introduced in v1.60.0 that breaks a documented CI/CD workflow. The --dry-run flag exists specifically to be consumed by automation — when its output format changes to human-readable text, it defeats the entire purpose and blocks CI pipelines that depended on it.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: install-deps --dry-run can no longer be used to generate install script
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v1.59.1 to v1.60.0. Broken commit: b25fbe4da0be34c9f04b8e092f08e0707fa24701. Specific CI workflow broken: separate playwright-build container that printed install commands for another container no longer works.

signals.topic: Reporter ignores NO_COLOR environment variable — ANSI color/cursor codes still emitted, violating no-color.org standard
signals.summary: Playwright reporter emits 38 ANSI sequences (colors + cursor codes) even when NO_COLOR=1 is set, due to internal FORCE_COLOR=1 override in worker spawn and NO_COLOR never being consulted in base.ts. CI tools relying on NO_COLOR convention get unwanted output.
signals.review_reason: Violates the no-color.org standard that has existed since 2013. CI systems and tools that set NO_COLOR to suppress color output are broken by Playwright. Clear reproduction with exact ANSI count evidence. Root cause identified in two code locations.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Reporter ignores NO_COLOR — colors and cursor codes still emitted with NO_COLOR=1
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows exactly 38 ANSI sequences emitted in B (NO_COLOR=1) vs 0 in C (FORCE_COLOR=0). Root cause identified: FORCE_COLOR=1 hardcoded in worker spawn overrides NO_COLOR per Node precedence rules; base.ts never checks NO_COLOR.

signals.topic: @playwright/mcp creates user data directories inside PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH — fails with EACCES on read-only filesystems (NixOS, Docker mounts)
signals.summary: MCP server writes browser profile data to PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH instead of a writable location. On NixOS, read-only Docker mounts, and shared filesystem caches, this causes EACCES permission denied, making the entire MCP functionality unusable.
aliases: MCP fails on NixOS read-only filesystem
signals.review_reason: MCP server is entirely unusable on NixOS and any environment with read-only browser caches — a common deployment pattern. EACCES error blocks the entire MCP feature. Concrete reproduction and root cause analysis provided.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: MCP createUserDataDir writes profile data to PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, fails when path is read-only
source_issues.evidence: Exact error: 'EACCES: permission denied, mkdir <PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH>/mcp-chrome-for-testing-<hash>'. Reproduced on NixOS and read-only Docker mounts. Root cause: createUserDataDir uses registryDirectory which resolves to PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH.

signals.topic: CLI daemon fails with EINVAL on macOS when session name exceeds Unix socket path length limit (104 bytes)
signals.summary: playwright-cli fails to listen on Unix socket with EINVAL on macOS when the session name pushes the socket path over the 104-byte sun_path limit. Common real-world repo basenames (>17 chars) trigger this reliably.
aliases: CLI fails EINVAL long session name macOS
Unix socket path length limit hit
signals.review_reason: CLI functionality completely broken on macOS for any non-trivial session name. Real-world repo basenames are the natural session identifier — users should not need to know about Unix socket limits. Clear root cause and path length analysis provided.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: playwright-cli open fails with EINVAL when session name is long on macOS due to unix socket path length
source_issues.evidence: Exact EINVAL error with socket path length analysis. 34-char session name triggers bug. macOS TMPDIR (~49 chars) leaves only ~17 chars for session name. Root cause identified in makeSocketPath concatenation.

signals.topic: VectorStore data persistence bugs causing SQLite upsert failures and Redis data corruption
signals.summary: SqliteVectorStore throws 'NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json' during UpsertAsync; RedisJsonCollection persists unannotated POCO properties into JSON payloads, causing incorrect data to be stored in Redis.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct VectorStore connectors have confirmed bugs that block core data operations. SQLite: UpsertAsync throws NOT NULL constraint error, completely blocking write operations with a database error that persists even with explicit non-null values. Redis: incorrect data (unannotated POCO properties) is persisted into storage, corrupting stored records. Both are production-blocking with no viable workaround through the SDK.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: [SqliteVectorStore] NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json during UpsertAsync
source_issues.evidence: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync throws SQLite Error 19: 'NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json'. The json column is defined as NOT NULL but connector serializes non-vector properties as null/empty, violating the DB constraint. Workarounds tried (explicit non-empty string values, relaxed schema) all fail. Manual SQL workaround bypasses the bug.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: .NET: RedisJsonCollection JSON upsert includes unannotated POCO properties
source_issues.evidence: RedisJsonMapper serializes the entire POCO record and only removes the key property, causing unannotated public properties to be persisted into Redis JSON payloads. This results in incorrect data being stored. The Redis JSON connector documentation incorrectly claims only vector-store model fields are serialized.

signals.topic: Handlebars template execution settings are ignored when PromptExecutionSettings object is provided at function creation
signals.summary: When creating a KernelFunction from a Handlebars prompt template with execution_settings defined in the template (max_tokens, temperature), providing any PromptExecutionSettings object during CreateFunctionFromPrompt causes all template-defined execution settings to be ignored. Only passing null for executionSettings preserves the template defaults.
signals.review_reason: Two related Handlebars template execution issues are confirmed: (1) template execution settings are completely ignored when any PromptExecutionSettings is provided, forcing users to choose between dynamic service selection and template defaults; (2) KernelFunctions from registered plugins are not invoked when referenced in Handlebars templates, blocking a core usage pattern. Both are confirmed bugs with clear user-facing symptoms and no clean workaround.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Handlebars Template execution_settings Ignored When Passing PromptExecutionSettings with ServiceId
source_issues.evidence: Providing any PromptExecutionSettings object (even with only ServiceId set) during CreateFunctionFromPrompt causes the entire execution_settings block from the Handlebars template to be disregarded. max_tokens and temperature from the template are ignored; execution uses AI service defaults instead. User is forced to choose between setting ServiceId dynamically or using template-defined execution settings.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Kernel.Invoke Function is not calling other functions specified in the prompt template
source_issues.evidence: When using Handlebars YAML prompt templates, KernelFunctions from registered plugins are not being invoked during kernel invocation. The kernel returns errors like 'cannot find current user time' instead of calling the TimePlugin function. This blocks the core plugin-in-template usage pattern.

signals.topic: Qdrant connector IsKeyPropertyTypeValid method not implemented, blocking collection operations
signals.summary: QdrantModelBuilder.IsKeyPropertyTypeValid is not implemented in the Qdrant connector, causing GetCollection and CollectionExistsAsync to throw errors. This is a regression from version 1.65.0 to 1.71.0-preview.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression: a previously-working method is now not implemented in the Qdrant connector, causing CollectionExistsAsync and GetCollection to throw errors. While count=1, the review_reason provides explicit user impact evidence: it blocks the primary collection discovery workflow, is a confirmed regression between versions, and was triaged as a bug. The P1 classification is appropriate for a non-blocking but clearly impactful regression.

source_issues.title: .Net Bug: Method IsKeyPropertyTypeValid in type Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.Qdrant is not implemented in 1.71.0-preview
source_issues.evidence: Invoking GetCollection or CollectionExistsAsync on QdrantVectorStore throws an error about IsKeyPropertyTypeValid not being implemented. Regression from 1.65.0-preview to 1.71.0-preview. This blocks the fundamental collection discovery workflow.

signals.topic: MEVD connectors use trimming-incompatible JSON serialization, blocking NativeAOT deployment
signals.summary: Memory-based Vector Data (MEVD) connector implementations use JsonSerializer.SerializeToNode in ways incompatible with NativeAOT/trimming, preventing removal of [RequiresUnreferencedCode] and [RequiresDynamicCode] attributes.
signals.review_reason: While count=1 and technically a design issue, the evidence clearly describes a user-blocking scenario: MEVD connectors cannot be deployed in NativeAOT environments because of trimming-incompatible JSON serialization. This forces users to either abandon NativeAOT or maintain workarounds, which constitutes a deployment/blocking issue rather than a minor improvement. P2 is appropriate for single-connector, non-regression impact.

source_issues.title: .Net: [MEVD] Stop using trimming-incompatible JSON serialization
source_issues.evidence: MEVD provider implementations (e.g. WeaviateDynamicMapper) use JsonSerializer.SerializeToNode() in ways that are NativeAOT-incompatible. This prevents connectors from being built with IsAotCompatible=true and forces retention of [RequiresUnreferencedCode] and [RequiresDynamicCode] attributes, blocking production NativeAOT deployments.

signals.topic: Custom PromptExecutionSettings properties not serialized into vLLM HTTP requests
signals.summary: Custom properties added to OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings subclasses (e.g. 'guided_regex' for vLLM) are not being serialized into the final HTTP request to the vLLM OpenAI API server, causing guided decoding to fail silently.
signals.review_reason: Custom PromptExecutionSettings properties are silently dropped during HTTP request serialization for OpenAI-compatible connectors. The vLLM guided_decoding feature completely fails because the custom property is never sent. This is a clear functional break in the extension mechanism for execution settings, with evidence comparing successful Python vs failing C# calls to the same endpoint.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Custom PromptExecutionSettings with 'guided_regex' property for vLLM OpenAI Api Server is not working
source_issues.evidence: Custom property 'guided_regex' defined in a VllmCustomExecutionSettings subclass extending OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings is not included in the HTTP request sent to the vLLM server. The server logs show guided_decoding=null instead of the provided regex. The feature works with Python's OpenAI client but not through Semantic Kernel, confirming the serialization bug.

signals.topic: Unsupported file upload renders conversation unusable (blocks continued use)
signals.summary: Uploading an unsupported file to a Codex Desktop conversation causes the thread to become completely unresponsive — the assistant produces no visible response and the session cannot be continued.
aliases: Conversation hangs after invalid file upload
signals.review_reason: Clear main flow blocking: conversation becomes completely unusable after a single unsupported file upload. User cannot continue the session at all — the feature is fully blocked.

source_issues.title: Bug: Unsupported file upload leaves Codex conversation unable to continue
source_issues.evidence: After uploading an unsupported file into a Codex Desktop conversation, the thread stopped responding. The conversation accepted the next user message, but the assistant produced no visible response. At that point I could not continue using the conversation.

signals.topic: CLI defaults to home directory instead of current working directory (regression, breaks project context)
signals.summary: After upgrading to v0.131.0, the Codex CLI ignores the current working directory and always opens in the home directory, breaking project context for all users working from subdirectories.
aliases: codex opens in home instead of current directory
signals.review_reason: Clear regression from v0.130.0 to v0.131.0. Codex CLI completely ignores the current working directory and always opens in home directory, meaning users lose project context every time they run codex from a project subdirectory. Main flow breakage confirmed by downgrade resolution.

source_issues.title: CLI always uses home directory as root in v0.131.0
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading to v0.131.0, running codex from the terminal does not account for the current working directory and always opens in ~. Downgrading to v0.130.0 fixes the issue.

signals.topic: Terminal/TUI corruption makes CLI unusable on Windows after MCP server startup
signals.summary: On Windows, upgrading to v0.131.0 causes the terminal to fill with raw ANSI escape sequences immediately after the codex_apps MCP server boots, making the entire CLI unusable.
aliases: Windows terminal filled with ANSI escape codes
signals.review_reason: Clear main flow blocking on Windows: the terminal becomes completely unusable (filled with raw ANSI escape sequences) immediately after MCP server startup. This makes the entire CLI product unusable on Windows after upgrading to v0.131.0. Confirmed by downgrade resolution.

source_issues.title: Codex v0.131.0 terminal corruption after codex_apps MCP startup on Windows
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading to 0.131.0, Codex starts normally but the terminal UI becomes corrupted immediately after: Booting MCP server: codex_apps. The terminal then fills with ANSI/control escape sequences. Downgrading back to 0.130.0 fully resolves the issue.

signals.topic: Git worktree Codex sessions interfere with each other causing session interruption and config errors
signals.summary: When a Codex session is active in a git worktree, launching Codex from another worktree causes a turn/start failure, and subsequent attempts to launch Codex fail with config path errors pointing to the wrong worktree directory.
aliases: Multiple git worktrees cause session conflicts
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for git worktree users: when a session is active in the base worktree, the worktree session gets interrupted and subsequent attempts to launch Codex fail with config path errors pointing to the wrong worktree. The session isolation contract is fundamentally broken.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI worktree session is interrupted when another Codex session is active in the base worktree
source_issues.evidence: Error: turn/start failed in TUI. After that interruption, Codex can no longer be started from the new worktree. Codex fails to start with: Error loading config.toml: Failed to read project hooks config file /home/user/projects/example/base-worktree/.codex/config.toml: Not a directory (os error 20)

signals.topic: Auto-reload credits fail to trigger when balance drops below minimum threshold, risking service interruption
signals.summary: Codex auto-reload credits feature does not fire when the balance falls below the configured minimum threshold, causing the account to run to zero and service to be interrupted despite the feature being active.
aliases: Balance hits zero despite auto-reload enabled
signals.review_reason: Clear user cost impact: user has configured auto-reload credits but the system fails to trigger purchase when balance falls below minimum, causing service to run out (hits zero). The core auto-reload feature is broken, directly causing unexpected service interruption and potential cost loss from forced downtime.

source_issues.title: Codex auto-reload credit does not trigger when balance is below minimum threshold
source_issues.evidence: auto-reload remains Active but no credit purchase occurs and credits remain at 1,000. Previously, when my weekly usage limit was exhausted and my credit balance crossed the configured threshold, auto-reload also did not purchase credits automatically. I hit zero instead.

signals.topic: Agent run aborts when model calls unknown/unregistered tool — no recovery path
signals.summary: When the model hallucinates or references a tool name not registered in the current agent, the SDK raises `ModelBehaviorError` and aborts the entire run. Long-running sessions cannot recover from this, causing complete workflow failure. Affects dynamically loaded tools and tools whose availability changes between turns.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed SDK bug causing main flow blockage. When an unknown tool is called (model hallucination or dynamic tools), the entire agent run is aborted with no recovery path. Author provides clear reproduction path through process_model_response(). This is a direct workflow blocker in long-running agent sessions.

source_issues.title: Make unknown tool calls recoverable instead of aborting with ModelBehaviorError
source_issues.evidence: Bug: SDK raises ModelBehaviorError and aborts the whole run when model returns a function tool call whose name is not registered. Path: process_model_response() -> build_function_tool_lookup_map() -> function_map.get(...) is None -> raise ModelBehaviorError. Author provided full repro steps.

signals.topic: Realtime tool invocation exceptions leave model waiting indefinitely — no output sent
signals.summary: When a known function tool raises an exception (e.g. timeout, user ValueError) in the Realtime agent session, no RealtimeModelSendToolOutput is sent back to the model. The model waits forever until the server-side ~30s timeout fires. Known-tool failure path is missing the output-send step that unknown-tool failures got in PR #3287.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed SDK bug causing session hang in Realtime mode. When a known tool throws an exception, the model receives no output and hangs for ~30s until server-side timeout. The fix for the same pattern on unknown tools (#3287) was already merged — the known-tool branch was simply missed. Clear code path evidence with repro script.

source_issues.title: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output
source_issues.evidence: Bug: known-tool exception branch (line 697) calls invoke_function_tool() without try/except. Exception propagates out and a local RealtimeError is emitted, but no RealtimeModelSendToolOutput is sent to the model. Model waits indefinitely (~30s server-side timeout). Author provides full repro script demonstrating model receives no tool output.

signals.topic: Sandbox LocalDir copy follows symlinks — sensitive files can be written into sandbox workspace
signals.summary: A sandbox LocalDir source can be validated as a safe local directory and then swapped to a symlink before or during the copy operation. This allows files from the symlink target (e.g. ~/.ssh/, /etc/passwd) to be written into the sandbox workspace, defeating sandbox isolation. Issue includes working exploit reproduction on current main.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed security vulnerability with working exploit. A validated LocalDir path can be swapped to a symlink before or during copy, allowing host system files (~/.ssh/, /etc/) to be written inside the sandbox. Reproduced on current main with specific paths (Path('src'), Path('.')). This bypasses sandbox isolation entirely, a critical security boundary failure.

source_issues.title: Sandbox LocalDir copy can follow symlink-swapped sources
source_issues.evidence: Security bug confirmed reproduced on openai-agents-python@65774ce8. LocalDir(src=Path('src')) and LocalDir(src=Path('.')) both allow symlink-swap that writes /workspace/copied/secret.txt. This defeats sandbox isolation by allowing arbitrary files from the host system to be written inside the sandbox workspace.

signals.topic: Voice text splitter silently drops short text chunks — no audio generated for short responses
signals.summary: StreamedAudioResult drops text when a custom TTS text_splitter returns a non-empty chunk shorter than 20 characters. Short responses like 'ok' are silently discarded even when the splitter explicitly marks the text as ready for TTS. The turn_ended lifecycle event is also not emitted when a custom splitter consumes all buffered text before _turn_done() is called.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed data loss bug in voice/TTS pipeline. Custom text splitters returning non-empty chunks under 20 chars are silently dropped, producing zero audio output. User sees no error — the short response simply disappears. Complete repro script demonstrates tts_texts=[] for 'ok' input. In voice-first applications, this means short acknowledgment responses produce silence.

source_issues.title: Voice text splitter drops short custom chunks
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed on SDK 0.17.1 and main at 92e014a4. Repro script shows 'ok' input produces {'tts_texts': [], 'events': ['turn_started', 'session_ended'], 'audio_chunks': 0}. Non-empty splitter output under 20 chars is silently dropped with no error or audio event.

signals.topic: Agent traces format changed between SDK versions — hierarchy harder to read
signals.summary: Traces from agent runs changed significantly between openai-agents 0.10.5 and 0.14.2. The new task/turn record format makes it harder to see sub-agent run hierarchy compared to the previous version. Users with established observability workflows built on the old format are now unable to easily interpret trace data.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed breaking change in trace output format between SDK versions. User provides visual comparison showing old format was more readable with clear sub-agent hierarchy. New format introduces task/turn records that obscure hierarchy. Users with existing observability integrations built on the old format experience a real degradation in debuggability. Not P0 since it's an observability/reversibility issue rather than a primary flow blocker.

source_issues.title: Did something changed with traces implementation?
source_issues.evidence: User reports trace format changed between SDK 0.10.5 (hierarchical, easy to read) and 0.14.2 (new task/turn records, harder to interpret). User included screenshots comparing both versions. Established observability workflows built on old format are now degraded.

signals.topic: Non-streaming calls hang indefinitely behind NAT gateways due to missing TCP keepalive on default httpx transport
signals.summary: Default httpx transport has no TCP keepalive (SO_KEEPALIVE off). During long non-streaming calls (300–700s for o-series/GPT-5.x reasoning), NAT gateways silently drop idle TCP connections. Client blocks forever, server completes the request, and no error is surfaced. Affects all cloud deployments (EKS, ECS, Cloud Run, GKE) and home networks. PR fix submitted (#3270).
aliases: NAT gateway timeout causes indefinite hang
long non-streaming requests blocked by NAT idle timeout
httpx default transport no keepalive probes
signals.review_reason: This is a high-severity workflow blocker: non-streaming calls hang indefinitely with no error, affecting all users behind NAT (the majority of cloud deployments). Server successfully completes work but client never receives it — a silent, total failure of the main API call path. Despite count=1, the pervasiveness (every EKS/ECS/Cloud Run user), the clear root cause, and the submitted PR demonstrate this is a critical SDK defect, not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Non-streaming calls silently hang forever behind NAT — default httpx transport has no TCP keepalive
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows [keepalive] completes in 604s while [no-keepalive] hangs forever. Server-side generation took ~606s, NAT dropped connection at ~350s. Affects all deployments behind NAT: EKS, ECS, Cloud Run, GKE, home routers. Dashboard confirms server completed the request.

signals.topic: SDK v2.34.0 breaks OpenAI-compatible local servers by rejecting empty api_key
signals.summary: In v2.34.0, AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError. This breaks compatibility with all OpenAI-compatible local servers (llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM, LocalAI) that intentionally pass api_key="" because they require no authentication. v2.33.0 and earlier accepted this silently. Workaround requires non-empty placeholder string, which is a surprising breaking change.
aliases: OpenAIError Missing credentials with api_key empty string
signals.review_reason: A single-issue breaking change that is a clear workflow blocker: local development with all OpenAI-compatible servers (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, etc.) is broken after upgrading to v2.34.0. This is a widely-used pattern for local development and testing. The regression directly blocks the main development workflow for a significant user segment.

source_issues.title: AsyncOpenAI(api_key="") raises OpenAIError in v2.34.0, breaking OpenAI-compatible local servers
source_issues.evidence: Root cause is new credential validation in _client.py line ~700 checking 'not self.api_key' (falsy for ''). Previously silent in v2.33.0. Breaks llama.cpp, llamafile, LM Studio, vLLM — all widely used. 2 comments from affected users indicating ongoing impact.

signals.topic: Streaming JSONDecodeError on SSE meta-only events (retry, id, event fields with empty data)
signals.summary: SSE decoder throws JSONDecodeError when encountering meta-only events (e.g., 'retry:' directives) per the WHATWG SSE spec. The SDK calls .json() on all events including those with empty data, causing crash. Fix submitted in PR #2721. Affects users behind proxies/gateways that emit SSE retry directives.
aliases: streaming crashes on meta-only SSE fields
SSE meta-fields cause JSON parse failure
signals.review_reason: Streaming crashes with JSONDecodeError for any user whose proxy/gateway emits valid SSE retry directives. This is a clear runtime failure that breaks the streaming call path. The SSE spec explicitly allows meta-only events, making this a definite SDK bug, not a misuse. It blocks production streaming workloads.

source_issues.title: Streaming: JSONDecodeError when SSE events contain only meta-fields (retry, id, event)
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly documented root cause: Stream.__stream__() calls .json() on events with empty data string (empty string from meta-only events), triggering json.loads('') which raises JSONDecodeError. Valid SSE behavior per WHATWG spec. Fix PR #2721 submitted. Long-standing issue since at least v2.6.1.

signals.topic: client.images.edit() fails to pass image_url as input, causing API 400 error
signals.summary: The images.edit() method does not properly pass image_url as an input field, causing the API to return a 400 error. The API documentation indicates image_url should be supported. If the API truly doesn't support it, the SDK documentation is misleading users.
aliases: images.edit() API 400 error with URL input
image_url not supported in edit endpoint
signals.review_reason: Image editing via URL is completely broken — API returns 400. This is a main feature failure for users trying to edit images without uploading files. Whether root cause is SDK parameter handling or incorrect API documentation, the user experience is a blocking error on a core API feature.

source_issues.title: client.images.edit() method failed to pass image_url as image input
source_issues.evidence: Passing a URL string to images.edit() (instead of a file object) results in a 400 API error. The API documentation claims image_url is a valid input format. Root cause unclear: either SDK doesn't pass the URL correctly, or the API endpoint itself doesn't support it — but the doc suggests it should work.

signals.topic: README "Nested params" example uses non-existent client.chat.responses.create method, is not runnable
signals.summary: The README 'Nested params' example calls client.chat.responses.create() which does not exist — Chat resource only has completions. Additionally, the parameters mix Responses API (input=[]) and Chat Completions (response_format=) surfaces. Users copy-pasting the example get AttributeError immediately.
aliases: README example mixes two API surfaces
signals.review_reason: README example is completely non-runnable, causing AttributeError for anyone copying it. This is a clear developer experience issue that wastes time and creates friction for new users. P2 because while impactful, the fix is trivial (documentation) and doesn't block core API functionality.

source_issues.title: README "Nested params" example calls non-existent client.chat.responses.create and mixes two API surfaces
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'Chat' object has no attribute 'responses'. The example mixes Responses API parameter shape (input=[]) with Chat Completions parameter (response_format), so neither API call would work as written. Direct user experience degradation for anyone reading the README.

signals.topic: Third-party skills introduce prompt injection, code execution, and safety gate bypass risks with no platform-level sandboxing
signals.summary: Multiple third-party skills in the registry have design-level vulnerabilities: wd1993/algorithm-solver feeds arbitrary user input into code generation then execution, yogesharc/supalytics exposes attacker-controlled UTM fields to agent context for prompt injection, and alltomatos/aetup-automatik bypasses interactive safety gates. ClawHub has no content safety scanning or runtime isolation for these third-party skill risks.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct third-party skills with confirmed design-level vulnerabilities (arbitrary code execution, prompt injection, safety gate bypass) indicate a systemic platform gap: ClawHub has no content safety scanning, sandboxing, or runtime isolation for third-party skills. Users who install these specific skills face real risk of data loss or unauthorized actions. These are not isolated incidents but a pattern across the plugin ecosystem. P1 rather than P0 because the impact is limited to users who specifically install these vulnerable skills, not a platform-wide outage.

source_issues.title: Security: wd1993/algorithm-solver feeds attacker-suppliable problem statements into code-generation
source_issues.evidence: Skill accepts arbitrary problem text, feeds it into code generation, then executes generated Python via Bash with allowed-tools: Bash, Read, WebSearch. No sanitization or isolation between user input and generated code. Arbitrary code execution risk.

source_issues.title: Security: yogesharc/supalytics returns raw visitor-controlled analytics fields (UTM, referrer) into agent context
source_issues.evidence: Skill returns UTM parameters, referrer, and page data directly into agent context. UTM fields are attacker-controlled and can inject malicious content that the agent acts on. Exposes Supalytics account mutations to prompt injection.

source_issues.title: [Security] alltomatos/aetup-automatik: Interactive safety gates (read -p) bypassed in agent context
source_issues.evidence: Interactive bash safety gates using 'read -p' are completely bypassed when executed by an AI agent, which auto-approves all prompts. Destructive operations proceed without any real human confirmation.

signals.topic: Legacy clawdhub@latest npm package resolves to broken 0.3.0 tarball, blocking installation
signals.summary: npx clawdhub@latest on a clean environment fails immediately with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, preventing users from installing the CLI tool at all.
signals.review_reason: Main installation path is completely blocked. Users cannot install the CLI tool via the legacy npm package path. Fresh repro with exact environment, commands, and error proves the failure is reproducible and blocking. Despite count=1, strong user-impact evidence (main path failure with full repro) justifies P0.

source_issues.title: legacy clawdhub@latest still points to broken 0.3.0 tarball
source_issues.evidence: Clean npm install (Node v22.22.2) with 'npx -y clawdhub@latest --cli-version' fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'undici'. Fresh repro provided with exact commands and error output.

signals.topic: Skill publish fails with 8192 token embedding error despite small SKILL.md
signals.summary: Publishing a skill to the registry fails completely with a token limit error even when the SKILL.md file is small, blocking the core publish workflow.
signals.review_reason: Core publish workflow is blocked for skill publishers. The 8192 token error fires on small files, indicating a bug in token counting rather than a legitimate limit breach. P1 rather than P0 because count=1 and no direct user impact evidence (no specific user blocked) beyond the title.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Skill publish fails with "8192 token" embedding error despite small SKILL.md
source_issues.evidence: Publish workflow fails completely with token embedding error. Title confirms small SKILL.md should not trigger 8192 limit. Source-repro and queueable-fix labels confirm maintainer acknowledges the bug.

signals.topic: clawhub install does not register skill hooks, causing silent functional failure
signals.summary: After running clawhub install for skills containing hooks/openclaw/HOOK.md, the hooks are not registered with the gateway. The skill appears installed in the UI but the hook never fires, making hook-dependent skills completely non-functional with no error message.
signals.review_reason: Critical functionality (skill hooks) is silently broken after installation. Users cannot tell the hook is not working — no error is shown. The skill appears installed but its core hook functionality is completely non-functional. Multiple clawsweeper labels confirm maintainer acknowledgment and the security/session-state impact labels further confirm non-trivial consequences.

source_issues.title: clawhub install does not register skill hooks automatically
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided: install skill with hooks, run 'openclaw hooks list' — hook is not listed. Skill appears installed in UI but hook silently does nothing. Security review label indicates hook bypass has security implications.

signals.topic: GET /api/v1/skills pagination never advances — all cursors return identical first page
signals.summary: The public API endpoint /api/v1/skills always returns the same first page regardless of cursor parameter. Passing the server's own advertised nextCursor back yields byte-identical response, making the entire paginated dataset inaccessible to API consumers.
signals.review_reason: Platform-wide API pagination is completely broken for all sort modes. Every API consumer (developers building on ClawHub) is affected and cannot access paginated data beyond the first page. The linked-pr-open label confirms maintainers are aware and working on a fix. P1 because count=1 but user impact is systemic across all API consumers.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Pagination not working on /api/v1/skills
source_issues.evidence: Full curl reproduction provided with exact commands. Both items[] and nextCursor are byte-identical between first request and cursor-passing request across all sort modes. A linked PR is open confirming the bug is real.

signals.topic: Chat attachments disappear after history reload or session switch
signals.summary: 用户在聊天中上传的附件在历史记录重载、会话切换或应用重启后消失，因为附件元数据从本地显示文本而非持久化结构化数据渲染
signals.review_reason: 核心聊天功能状态丢失问题，用户反复遇到（每次会话切换/重启）导致附件不可找回，属于关键功能数据丢失，bug标签+完整复现步骤支撑为真实用户痛点

source_issues.title: Persist chat attachment metadata across history reloads
source_issues.evidence: Bug标签明确标注为bug，有完整复现步骤，用户在切换会话或重启应用后附件消失，是核心聊天功能的阻断性问题

signals.topic: Toggling 'Allow screen recording' in Settings briefly hides left-nav items
signals.summary: 在设置中切换'允许屏幕录制'权限时，下游capability重新注册触发网关重连闪烁，导致左侧导航栏项目短暂消失
aliases: Left nav flickers when toggling screen recording permission
signals.review_reason: UI交互体验问题，切换设置项时导航栏闪烁，e2e测试捕获的真实问题，虽然非阻断性但影响设置操作的可用性感知，bug标签+完整复现步骤支撑
