aliases: Chat silently fails on incompatible gateway
No error shown when gateway lacks session key
signals.review_reason: 关键聊天功能静默失败问题，老版本网关用户遇到此问题后完全不知道原因，属于关键功能不可用且无错误提示的场景，用户影响明确但enhancement标签说明已识别为产品缺陷

source_issues.title: Show clear compatibility message when gateway lacks main session key
source_issues.evidence: enhancement标签表明是已知产品问题，需增强错误提示，用户实际遭遇了聊天失败但无反馈，是关键功能静默失败

signals.topic: WSL gateway validation uses stale/hardcoded tray output path causing validation failures
signals.summary: WSL网关验证脚本硬编码了旧的tray输出TFM路径，与当前构建版本不再匹配，导致验证失败或使用过时输出
signals.review_reason: WSL环境下网关验证工作流失败，硬编码路径与当前构建版本不匹配，直接阻断WSL用户的网关验证流程，bug标签+明确根因说明

source_issues.title: Fix WSL gateway validation tray output path discovery
source_issues.evidence: bug标签明确，WSL网关验证流程失败属于开发者工作流阻断问题，直接影响WSL环境下网关的正常验证

signals.topic: 106 empty try/catch blocks silently swallow exceptions, hiding real errors from diagnostics
signals.summary: 41个文件中存在106个空try/catch块，集中在DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue和事件处理调用中，实际抛出的异常被静默吞噬，诊断信息丢失
signals.review_reason: 异常静默吞噬导致真实错误不可见，用户遭遇操作失败但无诊断信息，deep-review审查发现但bug标签确认其影响，106处分布广泛影响多个功能路径的可见性

source_issues.title: [deep-review][duplication] D2: 106 empty try/catch blocks across 41 files (AI-slop pattern)
source_issues.evidence: bug+refactor双标签，deep-review为内部代码审查发现，但具体问题明确：异常被静默吞噬导致真实错误不可见，对用户而言表现为'操作失败但无反馈'

signals.topic: Android Play Store app (v2026.4.5) cannot pair against gateways >= v2026.5.12 due to protocol v3/v4 mismatch
signals.summary: Play Store Android app speaks WS pairing protocol v3 only; gateways >= v2026.5.12 advertise probeMin=4. Pairing fails with protocol mismatch, making Android Talk Mode realtime feature (changelog in v2026.5.18) unreachable from any released Android client.
aliases: Android app protocol v3/v4 mismatch prevents gateway pairing
Play Store Android client incompatible with newer gateways
signals.review_reason: Android pairing is completely blocked for any user on current Play Store app (v2026.4.5). Affects Android Talk Mode realtime feature advertised in gateway v2026.5.18 changelog. Two independent reports confirm the issue. count=2 meets P0/P1 threshold with dual-source evidence. Users forced to downgrade gateway to v2026.5.7 as workaround, losing 12+ days of gateway changes.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Play Store Android app (v2026.4.5) cannot pair against gateways >= v2026.5.12 — protocol mismatch v3 vs v4
source_issues.evidence: Gateway log: protocol mismatch client=ui v2026.4.5 min=3 max=3 expected=4 probeMin=4. Android app shows Gateway error: protocol mismatch. Both Play Store stable and beta channels at v2026.4.5.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Google Play Android app has an out of date gateway version
source_issues.evidence: Minimal report: Android onboarding fails at protocol mismatch step. Confirmed gateway version raised beyond what Play Store app supports.

signals.topic: Hook ingress token enables privilege escalation to full gateway operator on password-mode deployments
signals.summary: When hooks.token equals gateway.auth.password, a hook ingress bearer token authenticates directly to password-mode Gateway HTTP surfaces, bypassing hook-specific routing controls and escalating to full operator access including owner-only /tools/invoke.
aliases: Hook token reuse bypasses gateway auth boundary
Hooks token accepted as gateway password credential
signals.review_reason: Demonstrated concrete privilege escalation: hook ingress bearer token gains full gateway operator access on password-mode deployments. Not a theoretical issue — source code paths confirmed at auth.ts:550, http-auth-utils.ts:111, startup-auth.ts:224. Affects any deployment with hooks.enabled + gateway.auth.mode=password. PR is linked.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Hook ingress token unlocks password-mode gateway auth
source_issues.evidence: Hook ingress bearer accepted on password-mode Gateway auth surface; startup guard assertHooksTokenSeparateFromGatewayAuth() only checks against token mode, not password mode; security audit path also only detects token-mode reuse.

signals.topic: QQBot credential backups stored in home-global path, allowing cross-gateway credential import and identity collapse
signals.summary: QQBot persists credential backups to ~/.openclaw/qqbot/data/ instead of the active OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR. One gateway instance's credentials can be silently imported by another gateway instance sharing the same OS home directory, collapsing two supposedly isolated gateway profiles into one shared QQBot identity.
signals.review_reason: Architectural state isolation failure: two properly configured isolated gateways collapse to shared QQBot identity via credential backup path. Root cause is coupling to os.homedir() instead of active state resolver. Deterministic repro steps provided. Violates documented security boundaries. PR linked.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: QQBot credential backups bypass gateway state isolation
source_issues.evidence: Credential backup written to ~/.openclaw/qqbot/data/credential-backup-<accountId>.json by persistAccountCredentialSnapshot(); loadCredentialBackup() reads it back and writeOpenClawConfigThroughRuntime() injects into the importing gateway's config. Verified at channel.ts:168-295, platform.ts:42-45. Violates documented multi-gateway isolation model.

signals.topic: Heartbeat trigger spawns parallel claude live sessions that mis-route inbound channel messages, causing context-amnesiac fork replies
signals.summary: Heartbeat-spawned claude live sessions become eligible for inbound routing alongside the active channel session, causing user messages to sometimes be answered by a fresh session with no conversation history. Users see repeated fork replies appearing contextless.
aliases: Heartbeat creates parallel session that answers user messages with no history
Channel inbound mis-routed to heartbeat session causing fork replies
signals.review_reason: Main workflow actively disrupted: active channel conversations spawn fork replies from contextless sessions at every heartbeat boundary (~every 15min). Users observe apparent regressions in production threads. Gateway log evidence and PID evidence confirm parallel session issue. No workaround beyond accepting transient fork replies.

source_issues.title: Heartbeat-spawned claude live session captures channel user inbounds, causing context-amnesiac fork replies
source_issues.evidence: Gateway logs show activeSessions incrementing from 1 to 2 at heartbeat boundaries (every ~15min). PID evidence confirms two concurrent processes for same WhatsApp DM recipient. Fork replies reproduced 4+ times in single evening. Root cause: heartbeat-spawned sessions share reuse=reusable pool with channel-bound sessions.

signals.topic: Telegram group chats silently drop model text responses when model does not call message tool
signals.summary: When sourceReplyDeliveryMode is message_tool_only (default for group chats), any model text response that omits a message tool call is silently discarded with no error indication. Happens intermittently after long idle periods when prompt cache goes cold.
aliases: Telegram group message_tool_only mode silently discards text responses
Model direct-text replies lost in Telegram group chats
signals.review_reason: User-visible message loss with no error indication: model generates text replies that are silently swallowed by dispatch suppression logic. Affects group chat mode (the default routing mode for Telegram groups). Trajectory evidence shows 3 consecutive broken turns. Confirmed root cause in dispatch-from-config.ts. Silent message loss pattern matches P1 severity.

source_issues.title: Telegram group chat: model responses silently dropped when message tool not called
source_issues.evidence: Trajectory data shows 3 consecutive broken turns with isReasoning=false, toolMetas=[], didSend=false, non-empty assistantTexts. dispatch-from-config.ts silently skips payloads without deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression flag. Root cause: buildEmbeddedRunPayloads never sets this flag for plain assistant text.

signals.topic: Symlink loop causes aider to crash during repository scanning
signals.summary: When aider traverses directories containing recursive/broken symbolic links (common in cloud sync folders like MEGA, .cursor, Dropbox), pathlib.resolve() throws an uncaught RuntimeError, crashing the repo map generation and blocking the main coding workflow.
aliases: Too many levels of symbolic links
signals.review_reason: Two independent users on different platforms (Linux, different home directories) hit the same uncaught RuntimeError when symlink loops exist in their project directories. The crash occurs in get_repo_map(), which is called during the primary message-send flow, fully blocking the main coding workflow. Cloud sync tools creating symlink loops in project directories is a common real-world scenario.

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 990
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Symlink loop from '/home/kaira/Masaüstü/HAN/omni-reasoner/.cursor/hooks' — crashes get_repo_map() in base_coder.py during format_messages. User's working directory contains a .cursor symlink loop.

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 1239
source_issues.evidence: RuntimeError: Symlink loop from '/home/steve/MEGA/ea/EA' — same crash in get_repo_map() flow, different user on Linux with MEGA cloud sync folder. Confirms this is a recurring scenario.

signals.topic: tree-sitter QueryError crashes repository code analysis on Python module declarations
signals.summary: When parsing certain Python files containing 'module' node types in tree-sitter queries, an uncaught QueryError is raised in repomap.py, causing aider to crash during repository map generation — a core feature of the coding workflow.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users on different platforms (Linux and macOS, both Python 3.12) hit the same uncaught QueryError during repo map generation. The crash occurs in the core get_repo_map() pipeline, blocking the primary coding workflow. Both issues were closed with a comment referencing a known issue, confirming this is a recognized recurring bug.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module — crashes in get_tags_raw (repomap.py:302) during get_repo_map() on Linux with Python 3.12. Both closed with comment indicating a known issue.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: Same tree_sitter.QueryError on macOS with Python 3.12. Confirms this affects multiple platforms and is not an isolated environment issue. Both closed with same root cause.

signals.topic: litellm exception class not found causes aider to crash at startup
signals.summary: When litellm raises a new exception class (e.g. BadGatewayError) that is not in aider's hardcoded exceptions list, an uncaught ValueError is raised at message send, completely blocking usage. This is a startup/process-level blocker for any user whose litellm version introduces new exception types.
signals.review_reason: Uncaught ValueError crashes the entire aider process at message-send time, blocking the main workflow. While only one report, the root cause is a systemic issue: any new litellm exception class not in aider's list will cause this crash, making it a recurring high-frequency problem.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ValueError in exceptions.py line 66
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: BadGatewayError is in litellm but not in aider's exceptions list — uncaught at exceptions.py:66, crashes during send_message in base_coder.py. Affects every user who triggers this litellm error.

signals.topic: Pydantic version incompatibility blocks litellm import at startup
signals.summary: When a user's installed pydantic version is older than what litellm requires, an ImportError is raised when litellm tries to import its openai.py module, preventing aider from initializing entirely.
signals.review_reason: ImportError crashes aider before it can even initialize, completely blocking startup. The root cause is a dependency version incompatibility between the user's pydantic and what litellm requires. While a single report, dependency conflicts during installation are a known frequent pain point and the crash location (validate_environment) is a mandatory startup path.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in openai.py line 74
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'Discriminator' from 'pydantic' — raised when litellm/__init__.py imports litellm/utils.py which imports litellm/types/llms/openai.py. Crashes at models.py:validate_environment before aider can run. Windows user with Python 3.10.11.

signals.topic: SSL certificate configuration error blocks litellm initialization on Windows
signals.summary: On certain Windows environments, an SSLError is raised when litellm's httpx handler tries to create an SSL context, preventing aider from making any API calls.
signals.review_reason: SSLError crashes the process during litellm initialization, preventing any API calls from being made. This is a startup-level blocker specific to certain Windows environments with SSL configuration issues. While the root cause may involve the system's CA store, the crash occurs in aider/litellm's startup path and makes the tool completely unusable for affected users.

source_issues.title: Uncaught SSLError in ssl.py line 707
source_issues.evidence: ssl.SSLError: [X509] PEM lib — raised in ssl.py:707 when litellm's httpx handler initializes and calls get_async_httpx_client -> create_client -> get_ssl_configuration -> _create_ssl_context -> ssl.create_default_context(cafile=cafile). Windows 11 user. Blocks all LLM API calls.

signals.topic: rag-poisoning redteam 插件评估时抛出「Unknown grader」错误，导致所有生成的测试用例全部失败
signals.summary: 使用 rag-poisoning 插件运行 redteam 评估时，生成的断言类型 `promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning` 在 graders 注册表中找不到对应 grader，导致所有测试用例均以「Invariant failed: Unknown grader」报错结束，redteam 评估完全阻断。
aliases: rag-poisoning evaluation fails with Unknown grader error
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 是真实用户可感知的 bug：用户运行 rag-poisoning redteam 插件时，测试用例生成成功但评估阶段 100% 失败，错误信息明确（Invariant failed: Unknown grader: promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning），影响 redteam 功能的核心使用路径，且有完整复现步骤和源码分析支撑，置信度 0.95。

source_issues.title: Bug: `rag-poisoning` tests fail during evaluation with `Unknown grader`
source_issues.evidence: 生成的 redteam.yaml 中断言类型为 `type: promptfoo:redteam:rag-poisoning`，但 graders.ts 中未注册对应 grader，导致所有生成的测试用例在评估阶段 100% 失败（2 errors, 0 passed, 0 failed），redteam scan 流程完全阻断。错误可稳定复现，包括 minimal echo target 配置。

signals.topic: download_loader import fails from llama_index package breaking downstream integrations
signals.summary: When downstream projects (e.g., haystack-llamaindex integration) try to import download_loader from llama_index, they get ImportError. This blocks entire test suites and integration workflows.
signals.review_reason: Real ImportError blocking an actual downstream integration (haystack llama_hub connector). The entire test suite for the integration fails to collect, which is a main-flow break for users of the llama_index Python package. While labeled as 'question', the import error is a concrete, reproducible failure with a full traceback showing the阻断.

source_issues.title: [Question]: download_loader cannot be imported from llama_index
source_issues.evidence: ImportError when running pytest in haystack-core-integrations: 'from llama_index import download_loader' fails with 'cannot import name download_loader from llama_index (unknown location)'. signals.topic: SimpleChatEngine crashes with ValueError when ChatMessage contains multiple blocks during streaming response consumption
signals.summary: When SimpleChatEngine streams a response containing multiple blocks, the code attempts to set ChatMessage.content directly which raises ValueError. This crashes the application when consuming the streamed response and leaves chat history in an inconsistent state.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed application crash with full traceback: SimpleChatEngine's astream_chat path writes a multi-block ChatMessage to history using .content setter, which raises ValueError and crashes the consuming application. The bug is reproducible, has clear root cause (wrong API used in awrite_response_to_history), and affects a core chat engine path. Not P0 only because count=1 and no other independent reports confirming.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ValueError when ChatMessage contains multiple blocks in SimpleChatEngine
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed crash: astream_chat() returns StreamingAgentChatResponse whose background task writes to chat history. When ChatMessage has multiple blocks, awrite_response_to_history() does 'chat.message.content = final_text.strip()' which raises 'ValueError: ChatMessage contains multiple blocks, use ChatMessage.blocks instead.' The crash occurs at response.get_full_response() during streaming consumption. Full traceback provided. Affects llama-index-core 0.14.22.

signals.topic: Image download button in LlamaParse cloud UI is non-functional, blocking document integration workflows
signals.summary: The 'Download images' button in the LlamaParse cloud UI is permanently greyed out and non-clickable. Users who need embedded images from parsed PDFs to build markdown files with inline images cannot proceed, blocking their document processing pipeline.
aliases: LlamaParse cloud UI image extraction non-functional
signals.review_reason: UI-level bug confirmed by user with screenshots: the 'Download images' button in LlamaParse cloud is permanently disabled. While count=1, this blocks a key workflow (getting images from parsed PDFs into markdown files) for non-technical users who cannot code a workaround. Downgraded to P2 because count=1 and it is a cloud UI issue rather than core library breakage.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Download of images is not possible
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports the image download button in LlamaParse cloud UI remains grey/disabled and does not respond to clicks. Images display correctly in markdown preview and image preview, but the download action is entirely non-functional. The user is a non-coder who cannot work around it via API. Screenshots attached showing the broken button. This is the LlamaParse cloud product (cloud.llamaindex.ai).

signals.topic: CLI cold-install timeout blocks first-time users from running the tool
signals.summary: npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha cold install times out (30-60s SIGTERM) on cold npm cache, blocking MCP tool registration for first-time users and breaking verification checks in network-constrained environments.
signals.review_reason: Two verification issues independently confirm CLI cold-install timeout in different environments (30s MCP startup timeout vs 60s container limit). Blocks first-time users from registering any MCP tools — primary flow is actively broken. Both marked with verification labels and explicit severity, confirming real and recurring impact.

source_issues.title: [verification] MEDIUM: npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version times out at 30s (cold install)
source_issues.evidence: npx -y @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version consistently killed at 30s (exit 124) during cold npm install of ~911 packages. Blocks MCP tool registration. Workaround requires pre-install.

source_issues.title: [verification] HIGH: npx @claude-flow/cli@alpha --version times out in network-constrained container
source_issues.evidence: npx -y cold download of ~527 transitive dependencies exceeds 60s per-command budget in verification container, causing SIGTERM. Verification agent cannot confirm CLI version requirement.

signals.topic: Witness verification infrastructure broken — manifest drift and missing dependencies block integrity checks
signals.summary: Automated 12-hour verification runs report missing=95 artifacts and drift=2 on all platforms, plus signature verification fails due to missing @noble/ed25519 in source-only checkout, allowing real regressions to go undetected.
signals.review_reason: Two separate verification checks are broken: manifest integrity cannot be confirmed (95 missing artifacts) and signature verification cannot run (missing dependency). Both are in the automated 12-hour cron verification system. While manifests are currently valid, real supply-chain regressions would go undetected — a systemic integrity monitoring failure that could result in publishing broken artifacts.

source_issues.title: [verification] HIGH: witness manifests report missing=95 drift=2 on all three platforms
source_issues.evidence: All three platform manifests (macOS, Linux, Windows) report missing=95 artifacts and drift=2. Missing includes MCP tool bundles, CLI command modules, and security packages. If published, dependent MCP tool calls will fail at runtime with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The fix requires adding npm ci && npm run build to the verification environment.

source_issues.title: [verification] MEDIUM: Witness signature check unrunnable — scheduled runner lacks @noble/ed25519 (source-only checkout)
source_issues.evidence: Check 1 (Witness Signature Verification) fails with exit code 2 (precondition miss) because @noble/ed25519 is not installed in the source-only verification environment. This is not a real signature failure — the manifests are valid — but real signature regressions would go undetected until manual or CI-triggered run. Fix requires adding npm ci to the verification runner setup step.

signals.topic: Knowledge graph tools produce false results due to miswired/disabled controllers
signals.summary: kg-extract over-counts edges treating import type as value imports, kg-traverse reads from wrong storage tier and requires a disabled controller, causing phantom cycles and empty synthesis output with no error signal.
signals.review_reason: User following the canonical knowledge graph SKILL.md workflow gets systematically wrong results: phantom cycles, no semantic scoring, empty synthesis. Three independent bugs in the same skill bundle all fail silently without any error. Confirmed with exact version and controller state. This is a core feature producing fabricated output.

source_issues.title: ruflo-knowledge-graph: kg-extract over-counts type imports; kg-traverse references disabled/mis-wired controllers (3.7.0-alpha.69)
source_issues.evidence: Three concrete bugs: (1) kg-extract treats import type as equal-weight value import producing phantom findings⇄finding-actions cycles; (2) kg-traverse step 3 requires semanticRouter which is enabled:false in the binary; (3) kg-traverse step 6 reads from reasoningBank but kg-extract writes to hierarchicalMemory. User following SKILL.md exactly gets wrong results with no error signal.

signals.topic: agent_execute hardcodes Anthropic SDK — blocks OpenRouter/Ollama and ignores provider config
signals.summary: The agent_execute MCP tool and runtime ignore all provider configuration and hardcode Anthropic's SDK directly, making the entire provider config system non-functional for agent execution.
signals.review_reason: Provider config system exists but is entirely bypassed by agent_execute. User attempting to use OpenRouter (legitimate non-Anthropic provider) is completely blocked. Multiple config mechanisms (yaml, CLI set, env var) all fail silently. Clear user-impacting incompatibility with no workaround within the config system.

source_issues.title: agent_execute ignores provider config — hardcodes Anthropic SDK, unusable with OpenRouter
source_issues.evidence: agent_execute requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and calls Anthropic directly, ignoring: .claude-flow/config.yaml provider settings, ruflo config providers command (shows OpenRouter as Disabled even after enabling), ruflo config set (doesn't persist), and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL env var. User trying OpenRouter is completely blocked.

signals.topic: Subagent SendMessage/TaskUpdate silently fails in Claude Code harness — hive-mind coordination broken
signals.summary: Subagents spawned via Claude Code's Agent tool cannot access SendMessage/TaskUpdate tools, causing them to either abort with errors or silently produce stale/open-loop output without any hive coordination.
signals.review_reason: Multi-agent hive-mind swarm coordination is fundamentally broken for Claude Code harness users. Agents either abort or silently produce inconsistent open-loop output. The canonical CLAUDE.md SendMessage pattern is unusable for subagents. This defeats the core value proposition of hive-mind orchestration.

source_issues.title: Subagents cannot use SendMessage/TaskUpdate in Claude Code harness — hive-mind coordination silently fails
source_issues.evidence: 7-agent hive-mind audit: 2/7 agents aborted with 'SendMessage is not present in this environment'; remaining 5 completed only by ignoring the brief and working in degraded mode. Root cause: tool-availability asymmetry (lead has SendMessage, subagents do not) + no inbox/wait semantics for stateless subagents. Documentation promises SendMessage coordination but it does not work.

signals.topic: Failed daemon close leads to subsequent open reporting success but returning stale/wrong page content, silently corrupting AI agent data
signals.summary: After a failed `agent-browser close` (daemon already-dead), subsequent `open <URL>` calls report success (✓ <title>) but content queries return content from a previously-loaded page instead of the requested URL. The success message is derived from the target URL rather than the actual loaded page, so AI agents proceeding on the "✓ Done" signal silently read wrong content.
signals.review_reason: P1: Silent data corruption — AI agents trust the ✓ Done signal and proceed to read content from an entirely wrong page, without any error. This is a session state management bug where the daemon recovers to a half-dead state after a failed close, causing false-positive navigation success. Impact is severe (data corruption) even with count=1, and it directly breaks the core open → read workflow that AI agents depend on.

source_issues.title: After failed close, subsequent open reports success but returns stale content from prior URL
source_issues.evidence: open reports ✓ Done with correct target page title, but screenshot/snapshot returns content from a different, previously-loaded page (rustih.ru 404, Pasternak's «Февраль», Blok's poetry). Agent reads wrong content. Daemon is in half-dead state after failed close.

signals.topic: Headless Chrome helper processes leak and spin at high CPU after agent session ends, consuming multiple CPU cores
signals.summary: After agent-browser session ends or is interrupted, headless Chrome Helper child processes remain alive under a temp profile path, each spinning at 85–100% CPU. Multiple cores are saturated (~5–6 cores), draining battery and heating the machine without any visible indication of cause.
signals.review_reason: P1: Resource leak with significant real-world impact — multiple full CPU cores consumed silently after the agent exits, draining battery and overheating the machine. Workflow disruption since the user must manually find and kill the orphaned processes. This is an ongoing open issue with clear, high-impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Orphaned headless Chrome Helpers spin at high CPU under agent-browser-chrome temp profile
source_issues.evidence: Multiple Google Chrome Helper child processes each at 85–100% CPU, totaling ~5–6 saturated CPU cores. Processes did not disappear when agent/session ended; required manual kill. Temp profile directories left in ~/.openclaw/tmp. Previously observed as related to #1113.

signals.topic: Browser installation fails when `playwright` command is not found in PATH, leaving users unable to use the product
signals.summary: When installing agent-browser via Homebrew, `agent-browser install` fails with `sh: playwright: command not found` because the install script relies on an external `playwright` binary not present in the environment. Users are completely blocked from using the product.
signals.review_reason: P1: Complete product blockage — users cannot install the required browser and therefore cannot use the product at all. The install script has a hard dependency on an external `playwright` binary that is not guaranteed to be in PATH, especially for Homebrew installations. Multiple user reports (9 comments) confirm ongoing impact.

source_issues.title: bug: attempt to install the browser fails
source_issues.evidence: Installation command `agent-browser install` outputs 'sh: playwright: command not found' and '✗ Failed to install browser'. 9 comments indicating ongoing user impact. Users installed via Homebrew cannot install the required browser.

signals.topic: CDP eval/open silently operates on wrong execution context when DevTools is open, causing commands to appear successful on wrong page
signals.summary: When connecting via `--cdp <port>` with Chrome DevTools open on the same tab, agent-browser's Runtime.evaluate, Page.navigate, click etc. operate on a secondary execution context disconnected from the page's main world. The CLI reports success, eval returns coherent-looking values, but the visible tab is unaffected. `agent-browser doctor` also reports pass despite the misrouting.
aliases: CDP wrong context when DevTools open
eval targets phantom context with DevTools attached
signals.review_reason: P1: Silent command failure on wrong context — commands appear to succeed (✓ Done, correct-looking return values) but the visible browser tab is completely unaffected. This silently corrupts agent workflows where the agent believes a page navigation or click succeeded. The `doctor` command also fails to detect the problem. Reproduced on both Brave and regular Chrome.

source_issues.title: `--cdp` eval/open silently targets a secondary execution context when Chromium DevTools is open on the same target
source_issues.evidence: open 'https://example.com' reports success but visible tab stays on prior page. eval 'location.href' returns the prior page URL. Raw CDP on the same WS returns correct page. DevTools splits the CDP session, binding agent-browser to a non-default context. doctor reports pass despite the failure.

signals.topic: `--auto-connect` WebSocket verification times out in ~2 seconds before user can approve Chrome remote debugging permission prompt
signals.summary: When using `--auto-connect` with Chrome showing the remote debugging permission prompt, the WebSocket verification times out before the user or automation agent can click Allow. The auto-connect workflow is completely broken for headed Chrome scenarios requiring permission approval.
signals.review_reason: P1: Core workflow blockage — `--auto-connect` is designed for automated/unattended use but its timeout is too short to handle the Chrome permission prompt that headed Chrome displays. The entire auto-connect workflow fails in a common real-world scenario (headed Chrome requiring permission). This is a clear workflow blocker for automated usage.

source_issues.title: `--auto-connect` fails too quickly when Chrome asks for remote debugging permission
source_issues.evidence: Screenshot evidence of the permission prompt. Command `agent-browser --auto-connect open https://news.ycombinator.com/` fails before the user can click Allow. 2-second timeout is insufficient for human or automated approval.

signals.topic: generateText crashes with TypeError when experimental telemetry is disabled
signals.summary: When `experimental_telemetry: { isEnabled: false }` is set, `generateText.doGenerate` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total')` and crashes the entire call. This is a runtime crash in the core generateText flow triggered by an unhandled undefined reference in the telemetry record-span path, making the feature unusable when telemetry is intentionally disabled.
aliases: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total') telemetry
signals.review_reason: Core generateText API crashes with a TypeError in a user-intentional code path (telemetry disabled). This blocks the primary text-generation flow entirely. Stack trace confirms crash in generate-text.ts line 528, originating from the user's production call.

source_issues.title: Using `generateText` with experimental telemetry fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total')`
source_issues.evidence: TypeError thrown in generateText.ts:528 within the telemetry/record-span path when telemetry is explicitly disabled. Stack trace shows crash originates from user-facing doGenerate call.

signals.topic: streamText hangs indefinitely when fetch body is cancelled mid-stream (abortSignal not propagated)
signals.summary: When a streaming streamText or ToolLoopAgent.stream() call is aborted after response headers arrive but while the body is still streaming, streamResult.text and streamResult.steps never resolve or reject — they hang silently forever. The abortSignal does not propagate to streamResult, leaving promises dangling with no timeout or error path.
signals.review_reason: Stream text never completes when a request is cancelled mid-flight. Users have no way to recover from the hanging promise — it blocks the main streaming loop permanently with no timeout or error. This is a critical flow-blocking runtime issue.

source_issues.title: streamText / ToolLoopAgent.stream() silently hangs when fetch body is cancelled mid-stream; abortSignal does not propagate
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly describes streamResult.text and streamResult.steps hanging indefinitely when abort fires mid-stream. The promise never resolves or rejects, creating a silent memory leak with no error signal.

signals.topic: AI Gateway incorrectly translates ByteDance referenceImages causing upstream 400 error
signals.summary: When using bytedance/seedance-2.0 through AI Gateway with providerOptions.bytedance.referenceImages, the Gateway translates the referenceImages into the upstream content array but omits the per-item 'role' tag required by ByteDance's v2.0 ModelArk API. This causes a 400 HTTP error 'role must be specified for image contents', making the referenceImages feature unusable through the Gateway.
aliases: AI Gateway ByteDance role must be specified
signals.review_reason: Reference images feature is completely broken for ByteDance models routed through AI Gateway. The Gateway silently omits a required field causing upstream 400 errors. This is not a provider-side limitation but a Gateway translation bug.

source_issues.title: ai-gateway: bytedance/seedance-2.0 + providerOptions.bytedance.referenceImages fails upstream with "role must be specified for image contents"
source_issues.evidence: AI Gateway translates referenceImages to upstream content array but fails to add per-item role tag. Upstream ByteDance v2.0 API rejects with 400 error. User cannot use referenceImages through AI Gateway.

signals.topic: AI Gateway previousResponseId fails across Vercel-managed pooled OpenAI credentials
signals.summary: When using AI Gateway with Vercel-managed (non-BYOK) OpenAI credentials and previousResponseId for conversation persistence, the Gateway load-balances requests across a pool of OpenAI accounts. Since OpenAI Responses API IDs are account-scoped, previously returned resp_* IDs cannot be resolved on subsequent calls routed to a different account. This breaks conversation persistence entirely for users relying on it through AI Gateway.
signals.review_reason: Conversation persistence via previousResponseId is completely broken for all AI Gateway users with Vercel-managed OpenAI credentials. The root cause is the pool-based routing of account-scoped Responses API IDs. Users must switch to BYOK as a workaround, which changes their billing model.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: previousResponseId fails for OpenAI Responses API across pooled credentials
source_issues.evidence: Gateway returns valid resp_* IDs but subsequent calls cannot resolve them because requests are routed to different OpenAI accounts in the pool. BYOK resolves this by pinning to a single account. This breaks the Responses API persistence feature.

signals.topic: Cerebras provider produces wrong finishReason with tools and structured output combined
signals.summary: When using @ai-sdk/cerebras with both tools and structured output, the model's finishReason is 'tool-call' instead of 'stop' when returning the final structured result. This causes the SDK to raise an error since the output is used as if it were a valid structured result, making the combined feature unusable. A separate related issue (#15042) already exists for a different cerebras+tools problem.
signals.review_reason: Structured output is a core feature that becomes unusable when combined with tool calling on the Cerebras provider. The wrong finishReason causes SDK-level errors, making the primary use case of structured tool-use results fail. This blocks a key capability for Cerebras users.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/cerebras] Cerebras does not work with tools + structured output
source_issues.evidence: When agent outputs final structured result, finishReason is 'tool-call' instead of 'stop'. This raises an error when the user tries to use the output. The feature is completely broken — structured output cannot be used with tools on Cerebras.

signals.topic: App Router back navigation causes silent page unresponsiveness (hydration failures on Back button)
signals.summary: Multiple Next.js 16.2.x users report that after using the browser Back button, App Router pages silently fail to hydrate: buttons don't respond, scripts don't execute, and the entire interactive layer is dead HTML. Root causes vary (window.location.href hard nav, history.pushState, bfcache/restoration), but all share the same user-visible symptom: the page looks fine but nothing works. Affects both Turbopack and webpack dev.
aliases: App Router hydration on browser Back
signals.review_reason: Three independent users hit the same class of bug: back navigation renders pages visually intact but completely non-functional. Hydration is the core mechanism of any React app — when it silently fails, the entire interactive layer is dead. This is a main-flow regression affecting all App Router dev users on 16.2.x, and the lack of any console error makes it especially painful to debug.

source_issues.title: App Router (dev): `window.location.href` source page not re-hydrated on Back
source_issues.evidence: After Back navigation from a window.location.href hard nav, every interactive element is dead HTML. No __reactFiber keys on DOM nodes, no console errors. Works in next build + next start but fails in next dev. Affects both Turbopack and webpack dev.

source_issues.title: Scripts disabled due to cache error when navigating back via browser history (Regression) Next JS 16.2.6
source_issues.evidence: After Back button, all client-side scripts stop executing with zero console errors or warnings. Regression from 16.2.5 to 16.2.6. User describes it as 'major blocker for daily local development since history navigation is frequent'.

source_issues.title: Bug: `history.pushState` to a new URL reverts when route has a prefetched `<Link>` + `proxy.ts` cookie-based redirect
source_issues.evidence: history.pushState silently reverts to the previous URL within ~1 frame when the page has a prefetched Link plus a cookie-based redirect. URL flashes to new value then immediately reverts. RSC tree never reflects the click.

signals.topic: Vercel deployment fails with MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED — missing @swc/helpers/esm module at runtime
signals.summary: A clean create-next-app project with any middleware file and a static @sentry/nextjs import in instrumentation.ts builds and runs locally fine, but every Vercel deployment crashes with HTTP 500 and MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED. The missing module exists in node_modules but is not included in the Vercel function bundle. No workaround from the user side resolves it.
aliases: @swc/helpers ESM module not found on Vercel
signals.review_reason: This is a complete deployment blocker: production sites on Vercel fail to serve any page. The same code passes locally but fails in production, and the error provides no actionable fix path for users. The root cause lies in the Vercel-side bundling pipeline (not reproducible locally), making it especially hard for users to diagnose and workaround.

source_issues.title: MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED on Vercel deploy: Cannot find module @swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 500 / MIDDLEWARE_INVOCATION_FAILED on every Vercel deployment. Error: 'Cannot find module /var/task/node_modules/@swc/helpers/esm/_interop_require_default.js'. Module exists in node_modules. Local build and next start both pass. Affects both middleware function and page-render function paths. User spent 5.5 hours falsifying hypotheses — the crash is reproducible with a 3-line proxy.ts + one static Sentry import.

signals.topic: Turbopack production build hangs indefinitely at 0% CPU in SWC compile phase
signals.summary: next build with Turbopack hangs at 'Creating an optimized production build' with all workers at 0% CPU, retaining 4–9 GB of heap, and requiring kill -9 to clear. Intermittent (~1 in 4 cold-cache builds) but completely blocks CI/CD when it occurs. Only Turbopack mode is affected; --webpack builds complete reliably. Reproduced on both macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64.
signals.review_reason: CI/CD pipeline blocking is a severe developer-experience regression. The hang is silent (no error output), indefinite, and forces developers to fall back to webpack. Even at ~25% occurrence rate, this makes Turbopack-for-build unreliable for production use. The detailed heap retainer analysis and regression-boundary pinning make this a well-evidenced issue.

source_issues.title: Turbopack `next build` hangs at 0% CPU on 16.3.0-canary.21 — fingerprint matches PR #92210 (post-fix)
source_issues.evidence: Build hangs at SWC compile phase with 0% CPU and retained heap. ~1 in 4 cold-cache builds hang; other 3 complete in 4-5 min. Webpack builds are 4/4 reliable. Reproduced on macOS M2 and Linux. Root cause analysis points to a DashMap deadlock in task_cache. User must use --webpack as workaround, losing the Turbopack perf story.

signals.topic: Turbopack chunk filenames with multiple dots trigger WAF 403 responses in production
signals.summary: Turbopack's production build generates chunk filenames like 0od.e4.nsryo4.js (3 dots). Standard WAF rules interpret these as 'multiple file extension' attack patterns (like shell.php.jpg) and respond with 403 Forbidden. This causes ChunkLoadError at runtime and breaks the entire app for users deployed behind Cloudflare, AWS WAF, ModSecurity, or Azure Front Door.
signals.review_reason: Production deployment failures caused by a naming artifact in Turbopack's output are a significant cost-loss event for teams using both Turbopack and any common WAF. Users have no Next.js-side workaround and must abandon Turbopack-for-build entirely. This breaks a core promised feature of Next.js 16.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production build generates chunk filenames with multiple dots that trigger WAF 403 responses
source_issues.evidence: Chunks with 3+ dots return 403 from WAF/reverse proxy. Verified: 1-2 dots → 200 OK, 3 dots → 403. Causes ChunkLoadError: 'Failed to load chunk'. Affects all production deployments behind standard WAF rules. Webpack builds don't have this issue. No in-app fix available — users must remove --turbopack from build.

signals.topic: cacheComponents regression: not-found.tsx throws FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED in production instead of rendering custom 404 page
signals.summary: When app/not-found.tsx is invoked via notFound() in a layout with cacheComponents enabled, the production build throws a server error (FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED) instead of rendering the custom 404 page. Works correctly in dev and in non-cacheComponents configurations. Regression introduced between 16.2.3 and 16.2.6.
signals.review_reason: 404 pages are among the most fundamental features of any web app. Rendering a server error instead of the intended custom page is a clear main-flow regression in production. The cacheComponents dependency makes this a targeted but real blocker for teams using that feature, which is now default in Next.js 16.

source_issues.title: [regression] `app/not-found.tsx` throws FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED server error instead of rendering the custom error page when cacheComponents are enabled
source_issues.evidence: Navigating to an unmatched route in production (next start) with cacheComponents enabled throws FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED instead of the custom 404 page. Regression between 16.2.3 and 16.2.6. Does not reproduce in dev. User has 5 comments of active engagement and a Codesandbox reproduction.

signals.topic: turbo prune generates invalid lockfiles causing pnpm install --frozen-lockfile to crash
signals.summary: When using `turbo prune --docker`, pnpm lockfiles are generated with missing base package entries for peer-variant injected workspace dependencies, causing `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` to crash with 'Cannot use in operator' error in Docker builds.
signals.review_reason: Docker构建核心流程阻断：turbo prune生成的pnpm-lock.yaml无法通过frozen-lockfile验证，直接导致Docker镜像构建失败，用户必须绕过prune或修改lockfile才能继续CI流水线，影响所有使用pnpm+peer-variant注入工作区依赖的CI用户。

source_issues.title: turbo prune drops the base packages entry for peer-variant injected workspace deps, breaking pnpm install
source_issues.evidence: Pruned out/pnpm-lock.yaml missing base @repo/shared@file:packages/shared entry under packages:, causing pnpm install --frozen-lockfile to crash with 'Cannot use in operator to search for directory in undefined' at lockfileToDepGraph/headlessInstall. Repro provided with two apps pinning different react versions with injectWorkspacePackages: true.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker generates stale Bun lockfile causing bun install --frozen-lockfile to fail
signals.summary: Running `turbo prune --docker` generates a Bun lockfile that Bun considers stale, causing `bun install --frozen-lockfile` inside the pruned Docker layer to fail with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen'.
signals.review_reason: Docker构建核心流程阻断：turbo prune生成的bun.lock在裁剪后的工作区图中无效，bun install --frozen-lockfile直接失败，导致所有使用Bun的CI用户在运行prune后无法完成Docker镜像构建，必须回退到非冻结锁文件模式。

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker emits Bun lockfile that fails bun install --frozen-lockfile
source_issues.evidence: Pruned out/json/bun.lock is considered stale by Bun; running bun install --frozen-lockfile inside out/json fails with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen'. Minimal repro provided with two apps (api/sequelize-cli, front/eslint-config-next).

signals.topic: Schema URL returns 404 for released version, breaking IDE intellisense and turbo.json validation
signals.summary: The `$schema` URL `https://v2-9-14.turborepo.dev/schema.json` returns 404 Not Found, causing VS Code and other editors to show schema validation errors and lose intellisense for all turbo.json files.
signals.review_reason: 开发体验显著下降：schema URL 404导致所有IDE的turbo.json验证和自动补全功能完全失效，影响所有使用该版本schema用户的日常开发流程，属于关键辅助功能的不可用。

source_issues.title: Unable to load schema from 'https://v2-9-14.turborepo.dev/schema.json'
source_issues.evidence: VS Code JSON language server returns DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND when loading the schema URL. All users with turbo.json referencing the v2-9-14 schema see red squiggles and no validation/intellisense. Schema endpoints are hosted on Vercel deploys which get recycled.

signals.topic: Graceful shutdown completely broken on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
signals.summary: On Windows, `turbo start` kills all running tasks immediately on Ctrl+C instead of waiting for graceful shutdown, unlike WSL/Linux where tasks receive shutdown signals and can clean up properly.
signals.review_reason: Windows用户任务执行被意外中断：graceful shutdown机制完全失效导致所有运行中任务被强制杀死，在watch/dev模式下可能造成数据丢失、服务未正确关闭等问题，是明确的用户体验退化。

source_issues.title: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
source_issues.evidence: On WSL, Ctrl+C triggers graceful shutdown with 5.95s cleanup. On Windows PowerShell, tasks are killed immediately after ~1s with no cleanup. Repro provided with node script.mjs showing 'Aborted' immediately without 'Graceful shutdown end' on Windows.

signals.topic: turbo build causes 100% CPU usage and system freeze on large monorepos
signals.summary: Building a monorepo with 43+ packages using `turbo` causes 100% CPU usage and completely blocks the machine, while `pnpm -r build` completes normally with expected CPU usage.
signals.review_reason: 主流程性能严重退化：turbo build导致CPU 100%并完全冻结开发机器，使得开发者在大型monorepo中无法正常使用turbo，阻断正常工作流，用户被迫回退到pnpm -r build。

source_issues.title: Extremely slow with 100% CPU usage
source_issues.evidence: Monorepo with 43 packages: turbo build blocks the computer at 100% CPU usage, pnpm -r build completes normally. Perf profile attached. Affects Mac with pnpm and SWC builds with Prisma-generated files.

signals.topic: Next.js 16 PPR static routes fail lambda lookup during build when chain.headers is enabled
signals.summary: When using Next.js 16 with Partial Prerender (PPR) static routes that have `chain.headers` set (PPR resume header), the Vercel builder fails with 'Unable to find lambda for route' because the lambda key remap from `/route/page` to `/route` is bypassed, leaving lambdas stored under the wrong key.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow build failure (P0-level severity) that blocks deployment entirely for Next.js 16 users using PPR with 'use cache'. The root cause is a conditional in the lambda key remap logic that gets bypassed when chain.headers is set, leading to a deterministic mismatch between stored and looked-up lambda keys. Count is 1 (single repo), but the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: full build blockage for affected PPR routes.

source_issues.title: @vercel/next@4.17.1: static-PPR routes fail lambda lookup when Next.js 16 chain.headers is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with 'Error: Unable to find lambda for route: /foo' for all routes using 'use cache' with cacheTag/cacheLife that produce renderingMode: PARTIALLY_STATIC when Next.js 16 sets chain.headers. The builder's lambda key remap is skipped due to the chain.headers condition, causing lookup to miss.

signals.topic: DEP0040 punycode deprecation warning cannot be silenced in Vercel hosted builds
signals.summary: The deprecated `punycode` builtin module is bundled into the Vercel CLI launcher, causing a DeprecationWarning to fire on every hosted build in Node 22+. No user-side workaround exists because `NODE_OPTIONS` and dashboard env vars do not reach the launcher process itself.
signals.review_reason: While builds technically complete, the deprecation warning is present on every hosted build with no user-side suppression mechanism, causing persistent noise in build logs. The root cause is confirmed: bare require('punycode') in the CLI's eagerly-loaded entry path. The issue explicitly states no workaround applies to hosted builds. This qualifies as a recurring UX degradation that affects all users on Node 22+ hosted builds. Marked P2 due to count=1 and non-blocking nature (builds still succeed), but the evidence clearly demonstrates user impact.

source_issues.title: [CLI] DEP0040 punycode warning persists in hosted builds — user env vars don't reach launcher (follow-up to #11905)
source_issues.evidence: The warning fires deterministically on every hosted build, 7ms after 'Running vercel build' and before the CLI banner — meaning it's inside the launcher bootstrap, not a user subprocess. The NODE_NO_WARNINGS workaround only applies to local invocations, not hosted builds. Root cause: bare require('punycode') in CLI chunks resolves to deprecated Node builtin in Node 22+.

This is not a single security report — it's a recurring/ongoing operational problem for site owners whose real users get incorrectly blocked. signals.topic: vercel env add preview variable non-interactive mode fails despite CLI hint suggesting the exact failing command
signals.summary: Running `vercel env add NAME preview --value V --yes` (the command the CLI itself suggests as the way to add to all preview branches) exits with `git_branch_required` error instead of completing non-interactively, breaking CI/automation workflows.
signals.review_reason: This is a CLI workflow failure that specifically breaks non-interactive/CI use cases. The CLI's own hint/metadata suggests a command that it then rejects, creating a confusing self-contradicting UX. While count=1, the review_reason shows direct automation/CI impact: users cannot programmatically add preview env vars without falling back to raw REST API calls, which is a significant DX regression.

source_issues.title: vercel env add NAME preview --value <V> --yes returns git_branch_required despite hint suggesting that exact form
source_issues.evidence: The CLI's own error response includes a 'next[]' hint with the exact command that was just rejected, creating a self-referential loop. The command works interactively but fails in CI/automation contexts with --yes flag. The workaround requires using the REST API directly, meaning the CLI is fundamentally broken for non-interactive use cases.
